articles.title: Jonny Lomax: St Helens legend to retire at end of season
articles.summary: St Helens legend Jonny Lomax announces he is to retire at the end of the Super League season.
articles.body:
St Helens legend Jonny Lomax has announced he is to retire at the end of the Super League season.

The 35-year-old, who has not featured since fracturing his jaw in the defeat by Warrington Wolves in June, has made 388 appearances for Saints, winning five Grand Finals, one Challenge Cup and a World Club Challenge.

He won four caps for Great Britain and 11 for England, including a World Cup final appearance against Australia in 2017.

"Over the last 20 years, I have been able to live out a boyhood dream. Achieving far more than I could ever have imagined. Representing and captaining my hometown club and, of course, the pinnacle, representing England and Great Britain," he told the club website. , external

"I have been fortunate enough to meet some incredible people along the way, experiencing some incredible highs with them. As well as some testing times too."

He added: "I will retire at the age of 36, grateful for the life the game has given me, knowing I have given it everything I could, with the scars to prove it (19 operations, including 12 knee operations by the age of 26). Despite this, I still feel lucky.

"For those that have supported me throughout it all… I hope I have been able to do you proud."

Saints chairman Eamonn McManus called Lomax, who made his debut in March 2009 aged 18, "the bravest of brave in the bravest of sports".

St Helens are seventh in Super League with three games of the campaign to go.

They are two points behind reigning champions Hull KR, who they play in the final game of the regular season, as they look to secure a place in the top six and avoid missing out on the Super League play-offs for the first time.

articles.title: Can Connor McDavid equal Wayne Gretzky’s seven-season 100-point NHL record with Edmonton Oilers in 2026-27
articles.summary: NHL News: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid looks to match Wayne Gretzky's record of seven consecutive NHL seasons with at least 100 points. With six straight seasons already achieved, McDavid aims for historic consistency in the upcoming 2026-27 season.
articles.body: The Edmonton Oilers captain enters his 12th NHL season, reaching 100 points in each of the last six campaigns. Gordie Wayne remains the only player to have a longer consecutive 100-point streak, but Connor McDavid has established himself as one of the league’s most productive players.In the 2025-26 season, McDavid became the first player in the NHL to reach the 100-point mark, doing so in 60 games, and his next challenge is to carry that remarkable consistency into the 2026-27 season.Can Connor McDavid match Wayne Gretzky’s record this NHL season?Connor McDavid can become the first player in NHL history to have seven straight seasons with at least 100 points when he takes the ice with the Edmonton Oilers.Meanwhile, McDavid has six straight 100-point seasons and is one away from Gretzky’s seven straight. Gretzky scored 100 points in 13 straight seasons from 1979-80 through 1991-92, a record that still stands in the NHL.McDavid’s nine career 100-point seasons are tied for the third-most in NHL history. Gretzky leads with 15. Mario Lemieux finished with 10.In the 2025-26 regular season, he scored 48 goals and assisted on 90 for a total of 138 points in 82 games. The Edmonton Oilers finished second in the Pacific Division and made the playoffs, with him having at least one point in 68 games. He already had 100 points in just 60 games, ensuring another historic scoring campaign.How close is Connor McDavid to Wayne Gretzky?A 100-point campaign would match Connor McDavid with Wayne Gretzky for the NHL record with seven straight 100-point seasons. The Oilers captain has hit that number in each of the last six seasons and sits behind Gretzky’s record of 13 consecutive seasons, making the 2026-27 season quite special.Another 100-point season would put McDavid in the company of the elite in NHL statistical lore, alongside Gretzky. It would also bolster McDavid’s case as an all-time offensive great in the league.His personal resume already includes several Art Ross Trophy wins, Hart Trophy wins, the Rocket Richard Trophy and a Conn Smythe Trophy. McDavid also took home his fifth Ted Lindsay Award in June 2026.McDavid’s production will continue to anchor the Edmonton Oilers’ championship hopes. If he keeps scoring at this rate, it is going to have a big impact on where the team finishes in the Pacific Division and its chances to make the postseason.Edmonton Oilers star Connor McDavid is set to hit yet another historic milestone when the 2026-27 NHL season kicks off. McDavid’s seventh straight 100-point season would tie him with Wayne Gretzky for the most consecutive 100-point seasons. It would further put McDavid into the discussion of the greatest offensive players of all time in the NHL and add another milestone to his already phenomenal career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who is Kinley Rasmus? What to know about the record-setting LLWS star, her MLB dad and uncle
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus has captivated LLWS viewers in 2026.
articles.body:
In 2014, Mo'ne Davis exploded onto the scene, making herself one of the biggest stories at that year's Little League World Series. Over a decade later, Kinley Rasmus is putting herself in the same territory.

Rasmus, 12, turned in yet another record-setting performance Tuesday night, breaking the record for most hits by a girl in the tournament. It was the third record Rasmus has tied or broken during the event. In her first game, she tied Davis' record by recording eight strikeouts in a game . In her second game, Rasmus tied Davis for most strikeouts by a girl in a single LLWS.

With Rasmus' team — Phenix City — guaranteed at least one more game, here's everything you need to know about Rasmus as she looks to add to her already impressive LLWS resume.

If the last name Rasmus sounds familiar, well, it should. Rasmus is the daughter of former MLB reliever Cory Rasmus . Cory, who was selected by the Atlanta Braves in the first round of the 2006 MLB Draft, spent four seasons in the majors. Over 123 innings, he posted a 4.17 ERA. Cory dealt with multiple injuries over his time in the majors, which may have ultimately cut his MLB career short.

Following his MLB career, Cory became a real-estate agent . He currently serves as an assistant coach on Kinley's LLWS team.

Are you unfamiliar with Cory Rasmus? What about his brother — and Kinley's uncle — Colby Rasmus ? The 10-year MLB veteran was also a first-round pick, going to the St. Louis Cardinals in 2005. He reached the majors in 2009 and played for five different franchises over his 10 years in the pros. Rasmus posted a .241/.310/.436 slash line over his career, with 166 home runs.

Kinley plays for Phenix City, a city in Alabama. Though spelled differently, Phenix is pronounced the same way as Phoenix, the city in Arizona .

Phenix City's Little League team has quite a history with the Rasmus family, as both Cory and Colby played on the team in 1999, when Phenix City also made it to the LLWS.

Rasmus typically takes the field with her hair in a ponytail, which is held in place with a bow. At some point, that bow became a rallying cry for Rasmus and her supporters, and "Fear the Bow" became her unofficial slogan.

Rasmus talked about the phrase early in the 2026 LLWS, saying it brings her joy every time she hears it.

Entering play Wednesday, Rasmus has already set — or tied — multiple LLWS records.

Here's a list of her accomplishments so far:

• Tied Mo'ne Davis for the most strikeouts recorded by a girl in a single LLWS start with eight. • Tied Mo'ne Davis for the most strikeouts records by a girl in a single LLWS with 14. • Broke the record for most hits by a girl in the LLWS with five.

Since the LLWS began in 1947, only 26 girls have taken part in it. In addition to Rasmus, one other girl, Carsynn Meyer of Paseo Verde, is taking part in the 2026 LLWS. Meyer has already picked up a hit of her own at the event.

Despite Rasmus throwing six scoreless innings in her first start, Phenix City lost that game. Because of that, the team is just one loss away from elimination.

Phenix City rallied to win its next two games, and will square off against Great Lakes winner Hamilton, Ohio, on Wednesday in another elimination game.

During Phenix City's win Monday, Rasmus came on in relief to deliver 4 2/3 shutout innings. She threw 54 pitches in the appearance.

Because of that, Rasmus is not eligible to pitch again until Saturday at the earliest. In order to get there, Phenix City needs to defeat West Side LL on Wednesday. The team would then need to win one more game Thursday to give Rasmus another shot to appear on the mound.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Ray Garvin goes over best/worst case scenarios for these 5 polarizing players — See where he lands on them for 2026
articles.summary: Ray Garvin goes over ceiling and floor outcomes for five players going into 2026 fantasy football.
articles.body:
Every player has a range of outcomes. Some are tighter than others. Some are wide enough that the difference between the ceiling and floor can completely change your season.

That is what makes these five players interesting.

Each one has a realistic path to beating his current Yahoo draft cost. Each one also has something in the profile that can go sideways. So, instead of just calling them values or fades, let's look at the best-case scenario, the worst-case scenario and where I ultimately land.

Note: ADP references are based on current Yahoo drafts. Scoring is half-PPR.

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Chiefs — Yahoo ADP: 16.3 (RB10)

Best case: We all know this Kansas City offense has not looked quite the same since the days when Kareem Hunt was really rolling out of this backfield. The Chiefs have had good running backs since then, but they have not had this type of explosive runner in his prime. Going out and getting Kenneth Walker III tells me something about what they believe he can bring to this offense. He does not need to become Christian McCaffrey as a receiver. Give him the majority of the rushing work, involve him in the screen game and let Patrick Mahomes create scoring opportunities around him. Walker's ceiling pushes close to 20 half-PPR points per game. That is legitimate league-winning upside.

Worst case: Kansas City is thinking much more about January and February than your fantasy team. The Chiefs have multiple backs they can rotate, and the goal may be keeping Walker healthy for another Super Bowl run rather than seeing how many touches he can handle in September. Brashard Smith and the other backs remain involved, Walker loses some passing-down work and suddenly ,you're getting a good running back season instead of a great fantasy season.

My prediction: I'm trusting why Kansas City brought him in. I'm trusting Eric Bieniemy and I'm trusting that this offense needs Walker to be good. I have him projected as my RB6 while Yahoo drafters are taking him as the RB10. That's a gap I'm willing to attack. Walker is one of my favorite Round 2 running back selections this year.

Omarion Hampton, RB, Chargers — Yahoo ADP: 18.6 (RB12)

Best case: Hampton was already really good as a rookie. In the games he played, he averaged more than 15 fantasy points per game while showing exactly why the Chargers invested a first-round pick in him. He's big enough to handle volume, catches the ball well and now gets Mike McDaniel designing the run game around Justin Herbert. There is a lot to like here. My ceiling projection has Hampton around 1,850 scrimmage yards with 15 total touchdowns and roughly 17.5 half-PPR points per game. That is a top-eight fantasy running back outcome.

Worst case: We probably need to listen to what McDaniel is telling us. He's talked about this being a three-headed backfield with Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. Maybe that's coachspeak. Maybe it isn't. If Mitchell and Vidal are on the field more than Hampton managers want, his touch ceiling gets squeezed quickly. Add in another offensive line injury or two and suddenly that RB12 draft price becomes much harder to return.

My prediction: I'm buying Hampton even at the elevated cost. Sometimes good players in good offenses are worth paying for. He has the size, the receiving ability and a scheme that fits what he does well. Herbert should keep this offense moving and give Hampton plenty of scoring opportunities. There is committee risk here, but I'm willing to bet that the best back ultimately gets the most work. Hampton is one of the young running backs I'm willing to be aggressive on.

Christian Watson, WR, Packers — Yahoo ADP: 67.7 (WR28)

Best case: Watson finally gets volume to match his efficiency. In 10 games last season, he produced 611 yards and six touchdowns while posting a 17.8-yard average depth of target and 2.62 yards per route run. Romeo Doubs is gone, creating an opportunity for Watson to command the largest target share of his career. His ceiling projection reaches 111 targets, 75 receptions, 1,351 yards and nine touchdowns. That is about 13.3 half-PPR points per game and a massive return on a sixth-round investment.

Worst case: The volume never arrives. Watson has never reached 70 targets in a season and has played 14, nine, 15 and 10 games across his first four years. Green Bay also still has Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed competing for opportunities. My median gives Watson 99 targets, 62 receptions, 938 yards and six touchdowns. That's 9.5 half-PPR points per game and WR30 in my projections. If he misses more time or falls back into the 60-75 target range, the weekly variance becomes brutal.

My prediction: This is exactly the type of range-of-outcomes bet I like at this point in drafts. Watson's median is roughly fair value. That's not why I'm drafting him. I'm drafting him because there aren't many WR28s with a believable path to 1,300-plus yards and close to double-digit touchdowns. I'm willing to accept the volatility for that type of ceiling.

Rome Odunze, WR, Bears — Yahoo ADP: 67.5 (WR29)

Best case: I think people have been a little too hard on Odunze. He was playing really good football early last season before the year got away from him. He still finished with 661 yards and six touchdowns in only 12 games while averaging 10.3 half-PPR points per game. Now he gets another season with Caleb Williams in Ben Johnson's offense. Luther Burden III has also missed valuable time this offseason, giving Odunze even more opportunity to continue building chemistry with Williams. My ceiling projection has him at 117 targets, 75 receptions, 1,070 yards and 10 touchdowns. That's a strong WR2 season at a WR29 cost.

Worst case: Colston Loveland becomes that dude. That's probably the biggest concern for me. If Loveland immediately turns into the primary middle-of-the-field target and Burden is better than Odunze managers want him to be, suddenly there are a lot of mouths to feed. Cole Kmet is still around, too. Odunze can still improve as a player without the fantasy numbers exploding if Chicago spreads the football around.

My prediction: I'm bullish on Rome this year. My median has him at 110 targets, 70 receptions, 950 yards and seven touchdowns, which puts him at WR24 in my rankings. Yahoo is drafting him WR29. I'll take that discount. The Bears offense should be good and I want exposure to the receiver who has already spent two years building chemistry with Caleb Williams. At nearly the same cost as Watson, Odunze is the safer bet while Watson gives you the wider ceiling.

Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jaguars — Yahoo ADP: 83.9 (WR33)

Best case: We decide 2025 was the outlier. Thomas looked like a future superstar as a rookie when he caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. Last season was almost the complete opposite. His numbers fell to 48 receptions, 707 yards and two scores. The best-case scenario is simple: Jacksonville gets him back to doing what he does best. Push him vertically, let Trevor Lawrence attack downfield and stop forcing Thomas into a role that doesn't maximize his skill set. If we get something closer to rookie BTJ, he can destroy a WR33 price.

Worst case: Parker Washington actually becomes Jacksonville's WR1. That's not something I'm just saying for the sake of creating a downside case. I currently project Washington to lead this receiver room with 127 targets, 78 catches, 1,017 yards and seven touchdowns. Thomas sits behind him in my median projection at 104 targets, 61 receptions, 893 yards and four touchdowns. Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter also remain involved. If that target hierarchy holds, Thomas could once again be more volatile deep threat than weekly fantasy starter.

My prediction: This is the toughest one for me because the player has already shown us a ceiling that can make the current price look ridiculous. But I have to respect what the current role is telling me. Thomas is WR41 in my projections while Yahoo is drafting him WR33. If he falls another round, I'll gladly bet on the talent and the possibility that 2025 was just a bad season. At his current price, he's the easiest fade of these five players.

articles.title: Could Alex Nylander’s Calgary Flames tryout revive his NHL career after leaving the Toronto Maple Leafs organization
articles.summary: NHL News: Alex Nylander joins the Calgary Flames on a professional tryout after a successful AHL season with the Toronto Marlies, seeking to revive his NHL career. Can he prove himself during training camp and earn a contract?
articles.body: The Calgary Flames are inviting Alex Nylander to training camp on a professional tryout after a solid 2025-26 campaign with the Toronto Marlies. The move allows the 28-year-old winger to earn a spot on an NHL roster after spending the last two seasons within the Toronto Maple Leafs organization.He had 24 goals and 29 assists for 53 points in 65 regular-season games with the Toronto Marlies. He added six goals and one assist in 24 playoff games as the Marlies won the Calder Cup, so the Calgary Flames opportunity is a notable next step in his career.Why is Alex Nylander joining Calgary Flames for NHL opportunity?The Calgary Flames are bringing Alex Nylander in on a professional tryout, as his strong AHL production has earned him another opportunity to compete for a spot on an NHL roster, and, Nylander had career bests in goals, assists and points in the 2025-26 AHL regular season. His 53 points were among the top offensive numbers for the Toronto Marlies, and his playoff performance provided more evidence he can be a source of scoring depth.His impact in the postseason was particularly important. Nylander scored in overtime in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins, lifting the Toronto Marlies into the Calder Cup Finals.A pro tryout doesn't lock in an NHL deal for Nylander. Instead, it gives him a chance to compete for a potential roster spot during training camp and the preseason.The move provides the Calgary Flames a low-risk chance to evaluate a proven AHL scorer. The Calgary Flames finished the 2025-26 regular season with a record of 34-39-9 for 77 points and missed out on the Western Conference playoff picture. So adding competition for scoring roles could be useful.Why is Alex Nylander’s NHL return still uncertain?Nylander has NHL experience, but hasn’t proven himself to be a regular NHL player. He has 25 goals and 49 points in 126 career NHL games with the Buffalo Sabres, Chicago Blackhawks, Pittsburgh Penguins, Columbus Blue Jackets and Toronto Maple Leafs.The opportunity for the Calgary Flames is also huge because Nylander was born in Calgary while his father, Michael Nylander, was playing for the team. His older brother, William Nylander, remains a top forward for the Toronto Maple Leafs, adding another layer to the story.Nylander needs to show up in training camp and the preseason games if he is to convert his tryout with the Calgary Flames into an NHL contract. The opportunity is a direct shot at proving that his AHL season of 53 points can carry over into productive NHL production.Ultimately, it will be up to Calgary to decide whether Nylander offers enough offensive value to make the roster. For Nylander, it’s another chance to turn good minor-league numbers into a sustained return to the NHL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
São José-RS vs. Goiatuba-GO opens the Série D promotion play-offs this Wednesday Credits: @kelly_brolim /Sao José / @dkf_comunicacao and @eduardosoaresav/ GEC

The Brasileirão Série D promotion play-offs will kick off this Wednesday (26) with the match between São José-RS and Goiatuba-GO at 7 p.m. (Brasília time) at Francisco Noveletto in Porto Alegre. Tonight, the teams will begin competing for one of the two remaining spots in the 2027 Série C.

This will be the first match of the tie. Next Wednesday (2), at 7 p.m. (Brasília time), Goiatuba will host the return leg at Divino Garcia Rosa in the city of Goiatuba.

Nacional-AM and CSA-AL will battle for the other spot in the competition. They face each other at 9 p.m. (Brasília time) this Thursday (27) at Arena da Amazônia in Manaus. They will meet again on September 3 at 8 p.m. (Brasília time) at Rei Pelé in Maceió.

If the aggregate score is level after the two matches, promotion will be decided by a penalty shootout. All four play-off matches will be broadcast by Metrópoles.

Nacional-AM and CSA-AL compete for one of the spots in Brasileirão Série C Credits: Disclosure/Instagram/@nacionalfc1913 and @allaanmax/Disclosure/Instagram/@csaoficial

The creation of the play-offs is part of the overhaul that the CBF introduced to the men's professional football calendar starting this season, ensuring more excitement and competitiveness in the tournament. In the current edition, Série D featured 96 clubs, the broadest national inclusion in history, and awards six spots in next year's Série C. Four of these spots went to the semifinalists (ASA, Gama, Uberlândia and ABC).

The other two spots will go to the winners of the play-offs, whose participants are the teams eliminated in the quarter-finals.

articles.title: Register your pickleball team by Sept. 9 for the Fernandina Beach Fall League
articles.summary: Registration is now open for the City of Fernandina Beach Fall 2026 Pickleball League. The deadline for teams to sign up is Sept. 9th.
articles.body:
Registration is now open for the City of Fernandina Beach Fall 2026 Pickleball League. The deadline for teams to sign up is Sept. 9th.

The league is open to adults ages 18 and older, with a registration cost of $30 per team of up to four players. All matches will take place at the Central Park Pickleball Courts at 1200 Atlantic Ave.

Games are scheduled for Tuesdays and Thursdays from 5:30 p.m. to 9 p.m., weather permitting.

Play is structured into specific skill level and demographic divisions across both days. On Tuesdays, 3.0 Mixed Doubles games start at 5:30 p.m., followed by 3.5 Mixed Doubles at 7:15 p.m. On Thursdays, the 3.0-3.5 Women's League begins at 5:30 p.m., followed by 2.0 Mixed Doubles at 7:15 p.m.

All matches will follow USA Pickleball rules and pickleballs will be provided for participants.

Interested teams can sign up online through the city website , by phone at (904) 310-3350, or in person at the Atlantic Recreation Center, located at 2500 Atlantic Ave. Office hours for in-person registration are Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturday from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.

League competition begins Sept. 15 for Tuesday divisions and Sept. 17 for Thursday divisions.

articles.title: Craig & Chris Short end interim stint at Oxford
articles.summary: Oxford United confirm that former interim head coach Craig Short has left the club alongside his brother Chris Short.
articles.body:
Oxford United have confirmed that assistant head coach Craig Short has left the League One club alongside his brother Chris Short.

Craig Short took interim charge of the U's on three occasions in his six years at the Kassam Stadium, most recently for a period after Gary Rowett's sacking that included a 2-1 win over Southampton on Boxing Day last year.

Chris Short had two spells in United's backroom staff as head of sports science, first joining Oxford in 2018 and returning in 2022 after a spell away.

"Everyone at Oxford United would like to thank Craig and Chris for their years of dedication and professionalism," the U's said in a club statement.

"They depart with our sincerest gratitude and our very best wishes for whatever comes next."

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Has Limited Cell Service at Camp, but Says He Has to ‘Make Sure’ He Texts Wife Brittany
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes wed his wife Brittany in March 2022 and together share three kids
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes prioritizes texting his wife Brittany during training camp

The Chiefs quarterback credits his family and teammates for helping him stay grounded during his recovery journey

Head coach Andy Reid praised Mahomes' dedication to rehab after his season-ending ACL injury last December

Patrick Mahomes has his priorities in order.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback, 30, explained at a press conference on Tuesday, Aug. 25 that his phone time is limited during training camp , but that he always makes time to send a text to his wife, Brittany .

The topic arose when Mahomes was asked by a reporter if he's been texting Zach Ertz , the Washington Commanders tight end who the Chiefs QB previously praised for helping him through his ACL recovery, and Mahomes joked that the cell service in the cinderblock dorms they live in during training camp isn't up to par.

"I haven't been texting him during camp. I've been locked in throughout camp, but I know he's still working," Mahomes said of Ertz, who also suffered an ACL injury, one week before the Chiefs star. "I saw him throwing... I know he's working too."

"St. Joe's dorm rooms, man, you don't get a lot of text messages," Mahomes said of the rooms at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Mo., where they spend training camp. "I just try to make sure I text Brittany. If I text Brittany, I'm usually in a good spot."

On Aug. 5, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said the playcaller is spending " seven hours a day " working on his recovery since his injury. "He just goes. He kept playing, he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice, you know how he is — he's all in," Reid, 68, told CBS Sports at the team's training camp.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

"He's a great example to all the other guys around him that, 'I'm gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,' " Reid continued, noting that he and the organization make sure to "monitor" their star quarterback and work with medical staff to make sure he doesn't overdo it.

Patrick spoke with PEOPLE ahead of his return to the field for his 10th season in the NFL, and credited the people close to him — including his wife, Brittany, and their three children — for keeping him levelheaded during his recovery.

"Football is a huge part of my life, but I've always tried to keep perspective," Mahomes told PEOPLE. "Family, friends, my teammates, my foundation work, those things have always been important to me."

He added, "During the season you're so locked in, so having that time to slow down, be present with the kids, and just enjoy the people around you makes it special."

"I want to be the best for my family, my teammates, the kids who look up to this game," said the quarterback, who is looking to rebound after a disappointing 6-11 campaign last year that saw the Chiefs miss the playoffs for the first time in a decade.

"When I think about why I go out there and put in the work every single day, it's about being the best version of myself every single day so that I can have no regrets for how I played this game and went about my business," he said.

articles.title: ‘My joints just feel good’: Klay Thompson’s first reaction to life with the Heat
articles.summary: Klay Thompson signed a lean two-year deal with the Miami Heat and says the climate already has his joints feeling good.
articles.body:
Klay Thompson 's latest chapter began in Miami with plenty of attention surrounding the four-time champion. Just days after his Dallas departure became official, Thompson touched down in South Florida and was quickly asked about adjusting to his new surroundings. His response offered an intriguing first look at what awaits him with the Heat .

Thompson left $4 million on the table in his Dallas Mavericks buyout to chase a fifth ring in Biscayne Bay. Thompson's early reaction to the Miami climate proves he is already locked into the grind.

Klay Thompson explains why the Miami climate feels different

Thompson touched down in South Florida over the weekend, just days after his buyout with Dallas became official. Reporters caught up with him almost immediately, curious how the four-time champion was adjusting to his new city.

"My joints just feel good being out here with this climate," Thompson said in a video shared by ESPN. "I can't wait to meet staff, my co-workers, and executives, try new cuisines, get some really good local food, and get to work. I was always here in passing, so it's nice to be planted, just being able to experience a great place."

Thompson signed a two-year contract worth $11.5 million with the Miami Heat . He finalized the deal in August 2026 after agreeing to a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks . He gave up roughly $9.8 million to secure his exit from Dallas and join his new team. Speaking after the trade became official, Thompson explained his primary goal by saying, "The opportunity to win again at a very high level was so attractive to me."

Miami built this roster around a blockbuster trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo this summer, pairing the two-time MVP with center Bam Adebayo and now Thompson's outside shooting.

Thompson also addressed the demanding standard known as Heat Culture, saying some people mistake South Florida for golf courses and piña coladas when the program is far more militaristic. He added that he has been through harder things than a rigorous training environment, pointing to his lengthy recovery from past injuries.

Klay Thompson chases history on all-time three-point list

Thompson starts the season in fourth place on the all-time NBA three-pointer list with 2,899 made shots. He needs 75 more to pass Ray Allen for third place. This big goal is very doable in Miami because playing alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo will give him plenty of wide-open shots from the outside.

Bam Adebayo explained that Thompson's elite shooting will give the Heat the exact extra space they need on the court. Thompson has an amazing history, with four championships and a league record of 37 points in a single quarter. This means he will easily score if other teams try to crowd Miami's star big men.

With training camp coming up, Thompson trying to reach the top three in all-time three-pointers is a massive story in the league. If Thompson can make a lot of outside shots, he will give Miami the extra scoring power they need to beat the Boston Celtics .

Alexis Ohanian brought daughters Olympia and Adira to cheer for Serena Williams at the US Open

Serena Williams will reunite with sister Venus to play women's doubles after earning a wild card entry

The Williams sisters have won the US Open women's doubles title twice, and 14 Grand Slam doubles titles overall

Alexis Ohanian and his daughters are supporting Serena Williams !

On Tuesday, Aug. 25, the Reddit co-founder, 43, shared a few photos on his Instagram after he brought daughters Olympia, 8, and Adira, 3, to support their mom as she played in the US Open.

In the picture, Ohanian could be seen putting an arm around his older daughter, who was carrying her sister on her hip. After Williams lost in the mixed doubles quarter-finals, news broke on Wednesday, Aug. 26 that she would be returning to the court alongside sister Venus Williams for the first time since 2022.

The sisters won a last-minute wild card entry and will play women's doubles . Serena, 44, and Venus, 46, have won the women's doubles title at the US Open twice, in 1999 and 2009, and 12 more times at the three other Grand Slams.

This past June, Ohanian shared how proud their family was of Serena after she lost a three-set match during Wimbledon. The tech entrepreneur and father of two beamed with pride from the players' box as his wife returned to competitive singles tennis.

articles.title: Giants wide receiver Calvin Austin III out for season with ACL tear
articles.summary: New York Giants wide receiver Calvin Austin III is expected to miss the entire 2026 season due to an ACL tear he sustained at practice.
articles.body:
Aug. 26 (UPI) -- New York Giants wide receiver Calvin Austin III is expected to miss the entire 2026 season due to an ACL tear.

Sources told ESPN , The Athletic and NorthJersey.com about the injury on Wednesday. Austin hurt his right knee during practice a day earlier in East Rutherford, N.J. He was carted off the field at Quest Diagnostics Training Center.

Austin was expected to be the Giants' top slot receiver. Darnell Mooney , 2026 third-round pick Malachi Fields , Odell Beckham Jr. and Dalen Cambre are among backup wide receivers, behind Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton , who are listed as starters on their unofficial depth chart.

Braxton Berrios , Isaiah Hodgins , Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson are the other wide receivers on the Giants roster.

Berrios, cornerback Deonte Banks and running back Eric Gray are listed as the Giants' primary kick returns. Berrios also is listed as the Giants' primary punt returner, ahead of Austin and Gipson.

Nabers, who tore his right ACL and meniscus last season, shed his red non-contract jersey and participated in practice in a limited capacity Monday and Tuesday.

Coach John Harbaugh told WFAN on Wednesday that is "saying some prayers" that Nabers will be ready for Week 1.

"I've got my fingers crossed and saying some prayers too," Harbaugh said. "He looked good in practice, but practice is different than the game and all that. So he's gotta be comfortable and all the docs have to be comfortable.

"He's gotta look like he can do it and protect himself. But he's trending in the right direction and we'll see what happens."

Austin, who joined the Giants on a one-year deal in March, totaled 31 catches for 372 yards and three scores over 14 appearances last season for the Pittsburgh Steelers . The fourth-round pick by the Steelers in the 2022 NFL Draft totaled 1,100 receiving yards and 10 total touchdowns over the first 48 appearances of his NFL career.

NFL teams must reduce rosters to 53 players from 90 by 6 p.m. EDT Sunday. Nearly 1,200 players will lose their jobs before that deadline.

The Giants will face the rival New York Jets in their preseason finale at 7:30 p.m. Friday in East Rutherford, N.J. They will host the Dallas Cowboys on the same field in their regular season opener Sept. 13 at MetLife Stadium.

articles.title: Red Sox Provide Encouraging Curtis Mead Injury Update
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead before the trade deadline
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead before the trade deadline, but he injured his wrist in just his second plate appearance with the team.

Mead has been on the injured list ever since and has been in a cast. However, Tracy provided a positive update on the infielder before Tuesday's game against the Miami Marlins .

"He's healed enough, progressing in the healing where they could take him out of the hard cast and put him in the splint," Tracy said, per MassLive's Christopher Smith.

Getting out of the cast is a big step for Mead, but he still has a ways to go before he can get back in the lineup.

"He can start some mobility exercises," Tracy said. "So that's good news. It's still a ways off. He's been locked up for a while. So he's still gotta incorporate movement, mobility and strength. But he has moved on to that phase."

Mead was acquired to be the team's starting second baseman. He is under contract past this season, so getting him healthy goes beyond just getting him back on the field for a postseason run. The team traded Marcelo Mayer , so Mead is the preferred option at second base for the next few years.

Nick Sogard and Anthony Seigler have done a good job filling in for Mead. Andruw Monasterio has handled shortstop with Trevor Story out, but when Story returns, Monasterio will likely go to second base while Mead is still out.

Mead has a .851 OPS this season and is having the best year of his career. He has 17 homers and would be a huge boost to the Red Sox lineup if he can get healthy in time for the postseason.

articles.title: Dak Prescott has Cowboys fans worried after shocking practice moment at The Star
articles.summary: Dak Prescott sends Cowboys fans into panic after a scary training camp moment, but the veteran quarterback quickly gets back on his feet.
articles.body:
Dak Prescott is entering his 11th season as the starting quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys , and the expectations surrounding him remain as high as ever. Heading into the 2026 campaign, Prescott continues to carry the pressure that comes with being the leader of one of the NFL's most closely followed franchises, while also holding himself to the same lofty standards he has maintained throughout his career.

ESPN's Todd Archer shared some quick observations from the Cowboys' 14th practice, which was also the team's first session at The Star. One of the biggest moments came early in the team period when Prescott briefly caused concern across the facility.

On just the second play, Prescott appeared to get his feet tangled while taking the snap and fell to the ground as he attempted to hand the ball off to Malik Davis . He managed to flip the ball to Davis while going down, avoiding a potentially costly mistake.

Fortunately for Dallas, the scare was short-lived. Prescott quickly got back to his feet and showed no signs of being seriously hurt, immediately easing concerns from the coaching staff, teammates and everyone watching from the Ford Center.

Prescott also delivered one of the standout plays of the night. The best catch of the session belonged to tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford , who made an impressive grab in the end zone on a Prescott pass.

With a defender positioned in his way, Spann-Ford had to reach back to secure the football. Prescott deserves plenty of credit for the play as well, as he stepped up to avoid pressure and placed the pass in a spot where only Spann-Ford had a realistic chance to make the catch.

Premiership Women's Rugby says average attendances rose by 23.4% during the 2025-26 season, which concluded in June with Saracens winning a record fourth title.

The numbers have been aided by the boost the sport received by England winning a home World Cup at Twickenham in September 2025 and come despite the departure of United States star Ilona Maher from Bristol Bears.

Maher, who is the most followed rugby union player in the world on social media, generated unprecedented attention for the league during her stint in Bristol during the 2024-25 campaign.

The league also reported a 132% increase in social media following, a 310% growth in its database and more than 111 million views across YouTube, Meta and TikTok - a 174% increase in viewing figures.

Last season was the first during which every PWR match was broadcast live across platforms including TNT Sports, BBC Sport and YouTube.

PWR executive chair Genevieve Shore said the figures were encouraging given the high benchmark set by the 2024-25 season.

"Ilona's impact was extraordinary," Shore said. "It brought a huge amount of attention to our league and to our players, and we should absolutely celebrate that.

"So when you look at the fact that we have continued to grow from there, post-World Cup and after that incredible spike in interest, I think that is particularly encouraging.

"We can see growth across so many different areas of the business, and that gives us confidence that the work we're doing is truly connecting with fans."

The 2026-27 season of the nine-team PWR, which was launched in 2023 following the rebrand of the Premier 15s, is set to begin in November.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball Gives Anthony Edwards Fresh Chance to Cut Down on Ugly Turnovers
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have asked Anthony Edwards to carry the offense by himself on too many plays. He has brought the ball upcourt, made the initial mo...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have asked Anthony Edwards to carry the offense by himself on too many plays. He has brought the ball upcourt, made the initial move past his defender, and often had to make a desperation pass when the offense stopped moving.

Now LaMelo Ball gives Minnesota another guard who can start the plays. That addition could change not just how often Edwards loses the ball, but why those mistakes happen in the first place.

LaMelo Ball Gives Anthony Edwards Fresh Chance to Cut Down on Ugly Turnovers

Edwards averaged 28.8 points, 3.7 assists and 2.9 turnovers in 61 games last season. He also shot a career-best 48.9% from the field and 39.9% from three, so the issue was not that he was inefficient every time he handled the ball.

The bigger issue was the amount of work attached to those possessions. Edwards was often the player expected to create something when the first action failed, which meant more chances to score and more chances to make a mistake. That same burden was a major part of Minnesota's turnover problem last season.

That is where the new backcourt changes the conversation.

Ball put up 20.1 points and 7.1 assists for Charlotte last season. Now, he gives the Timberwolves a main ballhandler who can set up the offense and make that quick first pass to kickstart a play.

That takes a ton of playmaking pressure off Edwards . He does not have to create every single shot from the top of the key anymore, and now he can catch the ball after Ball has already forced the defense to scramble.

This change is significant and is more important than just reducing his turnover rates.

There is a massive difference between cutting down on turnovers and just making different kinds of mistakes.

When Edwards is the primary ballhandler from the jump, he has to face a locked-in, set defense and figure out a way to break it down. With Ball running the point first, Edwards gets to catch the pass after a defender has already blown their coverage or got pulled out of position.

That makes life way simpler for him. Instead of burning five seconds on the shot clock trying to cook his defender, he can shoot it, attack a closeout, or make the extra pass.

But do not expect the turnovers to vanish completely. Edwards is still going to attack the paint like a maniac, and heavy downhill drives will always lead to a few wild passes or lost balls. The real goal is to put him in better positions to take smart risks, not to turn him into a passive player who fears making mistakes.

This is where the new duo actually pays off.

A turnover does not always mean a player made a brain-dead read. Sometimes it is just the tax you pay when you force a superstar to bail you out with a junk shot late in the shot clock.

Minnesota needs to eliminate those ugly possessions. If Ball can initiate the offense and let Edwards attack a defense that is already scrambling, the Wolves give their best scorer a much easier mental workload.

That will boost his efficiency. Edwards shot 48.9% from the field and 39.9% from deep last year, so the real goal now is letting him hunt buckets without forcing him to carry the entire play on his back.

But there is one major catch to this whole plan.

Ball is definitely not some magic, mistake-free fix for Edwards' playmaking struggles. He coughed up 2.8 turnovers per game last season alongside his 7.1 assists, which shows how aggressively he tries to make plays.

So do not think Minnesota is suddenly erasing turnover risk from their offense. They are basically just shifting that messy responsibility onto someone else's shoulders.

That can still be a massive win, though, if it means Edwards spends way more time finishing plays in the end zone and less time trying to spark them from the backfield.

Chris Finch has to make the new backcourt work differently. If Edwards still has to take the ball out, start the action, and rescue every broken possession, then adding Ball will not change much.

The Wolves need a clearer order. Ball can organize the first part of the possession, while Edwards can decide when to attack after the defense has already been forced to move.

That is a much better use of both players, and it builds on the new job Edwards faces with Ball beside him.

The real test will come when opponents have seven games to study the Wolves' backcourt.

A playoff defense will try to make Minnesota's creators uncomfortable. It will decide which player it wants to help from, which action it wants to take away, and which passer it is willing to live with.

That is where the Ball-Edwards partnership has to prove itself. Minnesota cannot simply hope the two guards share the ball well. The Wolves need their new division of labor to produce better possessions when defenses become more aggressive.

Edwards does not need to become a point guard who makes fewer turnovers. He needs to become a scorer who is asked to make fewer unnecessary decisions.

That is the opportunity Ball gives him. The Wolves will know the experiment is working when Edwards' mistakes become less frequent, his scoring chances become cleaner, and the offense no longer depends on him solving every possession himself.

The Ector County ISD Athletics Department is honored, inspired, and energized by being named The Texas Way District of Distinction this summer. Only 39 Texas school districts received this recognition from the Texas High School Athletic Directors Association (THSADA).

"We are incredibly proud of our kids and coaches," said ECISD Director of Athletics/PE & Health Crystal Day. "This recognition reflects the intentional work they put in every day—not just to be better athletes, but to become better people and equipping them with tools for life that extend far beyond the game."

The Texas Way is a collaboration between athletic directors, coaches, and 2Words Character Development to improve sportsmanship at UIL events, decrease the number of ejections at these events, and strengthen communities and the relationships between coaches, athletics, officials, and fans, a news release said.

"Our families and fans are such an important part of what we do," added Day, who coordinates the district's The Texas Way efforts. "We want them to cheer loud, be proud, and enjoy the competition while helping us continue to create an atmosphere of respect and sportsmanship that our kids can be proud of."

To be considered for The Texas Way District of Distinction honor, school districts had to see equal or fewer ejections last year, strong engagement with The Texas Way Curriculum, community service participation throughout the year, and use of an intentional character development plan for athletics in addition to the Texas Way resources.

"For us, it's about so much more than winning games," Day said. "We are grateful that our coaches are intentional about teaching respect, accountability, character, and how to handle both the wins and the tough moments the right way."

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka's bold US Open look gets roasted by tennis fans
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka said she knew her daring U.S. Open would divide fans.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka's tennis skills weren't the only thing fans were talking about during the U.S. Open on Tuesday.

Her fashion choice also got plenty of attention.

The world's top-ranked women's tennis player stepped onto the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium alongside Novak Djokovic for a mixed doubles match against Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten wearing one of Nike's more daring looks for the tournament.

Think fishnet. Or mesh, depending on who you ask.

Sabalenka wore a black, see-through dress over a red sports bra and shorts. And apparently that still wasn't enough to make the look stand out.

The female tennis star added even more flash to the look with custom Material Good jewelry designed specifically for the US Open, including an 83-carat necklace, matching bracelet, and oversized drop earrings.

The jewelry was designed to match Sabalenka's personality and the energy of New York.

According to the designer, they wanted the set to feel "big" and "bold," while still being lightweight enough for Sabalenka actually to play in.

"We really work in tandem with her to create something very specific for her playing on the court and her vibe and style," Teresa Panico, the jewelry house's Director of Marketing, told " Town and Country Magazine ."

"She's very adventurous with her jewelry, with her style in general, but she's not scared of color and big pieces so we can get really fun and playful with it," Panico added.

Aryna Sabalenka's fishnet US Open look gets roasted by fans

Despite all the effort that went into curating the perfect look, social media critics quickly went after it. And they went after it hard.

"How about that - Sabalenka leading the parade of streetwalker chic at the US Open with fishnet over shorts and a sports bra. Why does New York bring out all the trashy-ness," one person commented on X .

"This is the biggest piece of trash kit I've ever seen in my life," another said .

"I'm sorry but this just can not be tennis wear… I'm embarrassed for her….and what's with the heavy inappropriate jewelry? New stylist needed pronto," someone else wrote .

"It's horrible. She looks like a trash bag," another person commented .

The good news is, the comments probably didn't hurt Sabalenka's feelings too much, as she said before the match that she knew the outfit wouldn't be for everyone.

"I love my outfit. If someone doesn't like it, it's okay. You cannot impress everyone with your outfits," Sabalenka said earlier this month . "That's why I like fashion because there is room for whatever, basically."

While she may have been prepared to deal with the internet fashion critics, the match itself didn't quite go as planned.

Sabalenka and Djokovic won the first set 4-1, Siniakova and Patten rallied to take the second 4-2 before dominating the match tiebreak, 10-2.

The loss knocked the top-seeded duo out of the first round of the U.S. Open mixed doubles match.

articles.title: Mississippi State cancels future road games at Memphis, Southern Miss, Tulane
articles.summary: Mississippi State backs out of the road leg of three home-and-home series.
articles.body:
With the SEC moving to a 9-game conference schedule, its teams are making adjustments to previously scheduled non-conference matchups.

For Mississippi State, that involves removing road games of previously scheduled home-and-homes. The Bulldogs scheduled home-and-homes with Memphis, Southern Miss, and Tulane but recently canceled the road trips for all three series .

Memphis and Mississippi State announced a home-and-home series in June 2020, where the Tigers were slated to host in 2028 and the Bulldogs in 2029. However, the series has been altered to a one-off matchup. Now, Mississippi State hosts Memphis in 2034 in Starkville, with no return trip to Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium.

Memphis won't even get a payout for losing its home game. Per the Jonah Dylan of the Commercial Appeal , the contract included a force majeure provision which allowed the series to be canceled without financial penalty if the SEC expanded to a 9-game conference schedule, which starts this year. Mississippi State replaced the 2028 road trip to Memphis with a home game against Louisiana Tech.

Memphis and Mississippi State last met during a 2021 and 2022 home-and-home series, where the home team won each matchup.

Southern Miss and Mississippi State announced a home-and-home series in February 2023, where the Golden Eagles were slated to host in 2030 and the Bulldogs in 2031. Similarly, the series has been altered to a one-off matchup in Starkville, MS, with kickoff moved up to Sept. 15, 2029. The programs recently held home-and-home series in 2014 and 2015 and again in 2023 and 2025, with Mississippi State capturing all four victories. However, the Golden Eagles are no longer scheduled to host the SEC opponent in the future.

Tulane and Mississippi State originally planned a home-and-home series in 2020 and 2023, but the COVID-19 axed the first leg of the matchup, and the series was moved to 2030 and 2032. Under the previous contract, the Bulldogs would host in Starkville in 2030 and the Green Wave would welcome Mississippi State to New Orleans in 2032. After recent revisions, the series has turned into a lone matchup in Starkville on Sept. 11, 2032. Mississippi State replaced the 2030 matchup with a home game against Troy.

The 2032 contest in Starkville will mark the first meeting between the Bulldogs and Green Wave since 2007.

Man City Ready £120m Enzo Fernandez Bid as Chelsea Face Deadline Call

Manchester City are preparing to make one of the biggest moves of the window, with TeamTalk reporting that a £120million offer for Enzo Fernandez is due to arrive in the coming hours. It is a deal with major consequences for both clubs, and one that appears to hinge less on City's willingness to spend and more on Chelsea's ability to react before the deadline.

According to the report, City believe the proposal will satisfy Chelsea's valuation. The complication is clear. Chelsea are only expected to sanction a sale if they can bring in a replacement quickly enough, a scenario that becomes harder by the hour as the window closes.

The latest line is that Fernandez is "understood to be keen on the switch" and interested in the opportunity to work again under Enzo Maresca. That detail matters. Player willingness can be decisive in late-window negotiations, particularly when a buying club is ready to commit a club-record fee.

Maresca's role also appears central. He has reportedly "been pushing internally for the signing" and City's persistence has now reached the point where the expected formal approach is imminent. TEAMtalk had previously indicated City retained strong interest despite an earlier deadline passing, and the situation has now moved into a more active phase.

There is a wider context to City's confidence too. The departure of Nico Gonzalez to Newcastle United has opened space, while movement elsewhere in the squad has preserved flexibility for another senior midfield addition. In practical terms, it means City feel able to justify a move of this scale so late in the market.

Chelsea's position is more complex. The report states that "That condition remains the principal obstacle", with the club needing to identify and secure a suitable successor before agreeing to part with a major midfield asset. Even with £120million on the table, there is no certainty they can execute that plan in time.

The names mentioned are significant. Bournemouth 's Alex Scott and Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton are both admired, though both would be costly and difficult to prise away at this stage. Monaco 's Lamine Camara is another option under consideration, but this is exactly why the next phase matters so much. If Chelsea cannot progress on alternatives, then, as reported, "the bid may be rejected regardless of the fee."

If completed, the move would eclipse the £116million City paid for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer, making Fernandez the club's record signing. That in itself tells the story. City are not probing here, they are testing Chelsea with a number designed to force a genuine decision.

For now, the report suggests "both Fernandez's desire and Maresca's push have kept the possibility of a move to City alive." That leaves this transfer balanced between intent and timing, with the final hours likely to determine whether one of the window's biggest stories becomes a completed deal.

From a hopeful Manchester City perspective, this feels like the sort of move that could reshape the midfield for years. Fernandez has the intensity, passing range and personality to thrive in a side that expects to dominate matches and compete for the biggest honours. If there is genuine willingness from the player, and if the manager truly sees him as a priority, then City supporters will naturally feel encouraged.

The £120million figure is enormous, but elite midfielders in the right age bracket rarely come onto the market without huge cost attached. If the club believe he is the right fit, there is logic in being bold. His profile suggests someone capable of dictating tempo, handling pressure and adding competitive edge in major games.

There will be understandable concern over the fee and whether Chelsea can still block the move by failing to land a replacement. Yet from a City fan's point of view, the important part is that the club seem ready to act decisively. After squad changes this summer, another top-level midfield arrival would send a powerful message.

Supporters will also like the idea that this is being driven by conviction rather than opportunity alone. If Maresca has really "been pushing internally for the signing", that suggests a defined tactical plan. In the end, that is what gives this story real substance. For City fans, there is every reason to watch the next few hours with optimism.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: How to evaluate post-hype sleepers and identifying upside players the market has left behind for 2026
articles.summary: Chris Allen looks at players who hit their low point but could see the sunlight again in 2026.
articles.body:
I know I can be stubborn. First of all, don't tell my wife. She already "knows" this, but I'll never say it out loud (and I still haven't!). I'll come up with an idea or learn a theory, see proof of concept one (1) time and latch onto the notion. Anyway, second, I'd like to believe it's part of human nature.

You couldn't change my mind about the Bengals outlook in 2021. Joe Burrow's shortened rookie campaign was enough. And they added his best friend and phenom to run alongside Tee Higgins? Just tell me when they schedule the parade in Cincinnati. And yet, each year, we have the same discussions regarding their claim to a postseason slot.

Post-hype sleepers command similar discourse in fantasy circles. They're players we know have played well or showed enough flashes, but flopped once the collective community took interest. A few hit their low point in 2025. But let's see if they're worth a click in drafts this year.

Much to my own chagrin, let's expand on my Bengals analogy.

Typically, post-hype sleepers operate on a three-year cycle. The market values them (slightly) below their original ADP. For rookies, we've got historical benchmarks on collegiate production and draft capital to guide us. Vets can follow a different arc, but we'll get to them. In either case, the value, even the slightest edge in results relative to cost, is enough for us to push their draft price ahead the following season.

But that doesn't always equate to an equal rise in generated points.

I went through the last 10 years of data to isolate post-hype sleepers in fantasy. It was like walking down Memory Lane of my worst decisions. Regardless, a couple of takeaways here.

First, when things went bad for players, they were catastrophic for fantasy managers. The median drop between ADP and end-of-season ranks was 24 spots across all positions. WRs took the brunt of the collapse (average drop of 44.2). Quarterbacks had the mildest decline (14.7). The impact would pull your team out of playoff contention without an in-season roster adjustment. But the larger point lies in the two bars over the "Discount Year."

Even when we find the guys with the (past) talent to outkick their ADP, us being right is only a minor win. In other words, the hype pulls us out a bit too far over our skis. Think about the Malik Nabers' buildup going on now. If healthy, he'd be a first-round pick after an electric rookie year. Accordingly, you can almost hear his price creep up with every positive piece of news.

But again, our evaluation of his situation (i.e., health) doesn't mean Nabers will be a WR1 again. And that's been the case for RBs and TEs, too. However, we've been able to make successful bets in the past.

The hit rate on post-hype sleepers for three of the four skill positions sits at about a coin flip. So, despite the potential for a slight loss in value, there's upside in targeting the guys we think the market has left behind.

Admittedly, RBs have a tougher draw. But in most cases, we can see the outcome before opening kickoff. Only 9.1% of the running backs over 26 years old with post-hype sleeper appeal exceeded their draft cost. On the flip side, this data point gives us a partial framework to dig into this year's candidates.

Speaking of, let's kick things off with a passer carrying some uncertainty into 2026.

The Talent Never Left, Just the Health Bar

I'll be upfront. I have no dog in the "J.J. McCarthy should be QB1" fight. HC Kevin O'Connell made his decision to make Kyler Murray the starter. But at QB16, gamers have to figure out if there's any juice to squeeze out of the cost. I say, yes.

Now, one pass in a joint preseason practice has as much relevance to the regular season as this article. But we've been able to catch glimpses of Murray connecting with his ancillary pass-catchers . He's also started reinforcing the idea that Justin Jefferson could be back in the WR1 discussion by season's end. Regardless, Vikings fans (and fantasy managers) are expecting an upgrade from 2025. And based on history, we're right to demand more from the offense.

EPA per Dropback: 0.05 (Murray, career), -0.14 (McCarthy, 2025)

Three stats don't define a QB, but we can start the conversation here. While Murray hasn't been the most efficient thrower, his ability to avoid catastrophic plays (e.g., sacks, turnovers) puts him ahead of his current competition in Minnesota. And let's keep in context that the Cardinals' offensive line was deteriorating to a similar state as the Vikings. Murray was up to a 34.5% pressure rate in 2025. But unlike McCarthy, Murray brings some mobility to the position.

2022: 14.2% (rushing rate), 7th (among all QBs, min. 200 dropbacks)

Even during injury-riddled years, Murray's rushing rate (combination of scrambles and designed runs) has been inside the top 12. Now, he's piloting an offense with a playcaller who's historically integrated high-pace, play-action concepts and pre-snap motion (easy buttons for QBs) at or above the league average since joining the Vikings. While quarterback may seem deep once you get into the middle and late rounds, if I'm looking for upside, Murray fits the archetype of a passer that can finish as a QB1 in 2026.

As the previous data indicated, finding post-hype sleeper RBs is harder than it sounds. There are more losses than wins for those hoping they'll recapture some magic from their rusher's best season. However, the guys that have done it give us an idea of where to look.

Unsurprisingly, good runners tend to stay good. Box score scouts will check total yards or cite yards per carry, but context is everything. Per-touch metrics tend to hold steady for RBs even in their down year. Essentially, the production wanes but their talent doesn't. You might shake your head at the notion, but look at how often coaches (i.e., people with more knowledge of the situation than me) decided to give those same runners the ball.

Again, not a lot of change. Ball carries saw an average drop of 2.6% percentage points across the opportunity stats most conducive to fantasy scoring. Said another way, if teams felt like their preseason evaluation was wrong, they'd fix it! We'd see a timeshare form before the word "committee" left our lips. I can think of one guy for 2026 that fits, but it may be a stretch.

Bucky Irving became everyone's favorite RB to target in drafts after 2024. The Oregon product dominated the Bucs' backfield in early-down rushing success rate and forced missed tackles. While also edging out Rachaad White in targets, it became clear who had the juice to take over the following year. But then disaster struck.

YAC per Att.: 4.03 (2024), 2.39 (2025, Weeks 1-4)

Good news, Irving opened the year as the RB1. Bad news: early-season returns were disappointing. He scored two touchdowns in the first month. Despite the boosted workload, it took until Week 4 for us to get a "vintage" Irving performance. However, there are a few hints as to why.

Baker Mayfield: sprained MCL, PCL, and bone bruise from Week 2; suffered a bicep contusion in Week 3; AC joint sprain in Week 12.

Offensive line injuries: Two starters missed time during the first month; nine different starting rotations used throughout the year.

Irving wasn't the only Buccaneer dealing with ailments. Again, they're not the sole explanation for the decline, but a reasonable contributor to most of it. Sure, the addition of Kenneth Gainwell will provide another challenge for Irving as a receiver and short-yardage option. Still, an improvement in offensive situation should be enough to buy into Irving again.

Fortunately, the same general logic applies for receivers who we think have a chance to bounce back after a down year. Their volume remains the same, if not better, along with their efficiency. But something outside of their control slashes their productivity. So, when I saw the 49ers prioritize signing a new WR to their corps, I took notice.

Let's look at Mike Evans' usage between 2024 and the earlier parts of last season. I know he was injured most of '25, but we should at least establish the same pattern of a continued high-end workload.

For a guy with a couple of young(er) bucks coming after his job, Evans was holding his own. Prior to injury, the 33-year-old was Baker Mayfield's top option. And Evans put the receptions to good use, leading the team in air yards and first downs per route run. So, on the positive side, he showed he could still compete. But it was still a step down from the year before.

First Downs per Route Run: 12.9% (2024), 10.3% (2025, Weeks 1-3)

Yards After the Catch per Reception: 2.98, 1.30

Now, I'm not expecting a WR over the age of 30 to still be fleet of foot. That's where on-field deployment should evolve. But Evans played alongside Emeka Egbuka and Sterling Shepard. Neither of whom could reliably operate as the X-receiver. To make matters worse, as Mayfield picked up injuries, his ability to connect with his main guy plummeted.

Completion % (on throws outside the numbers): 59.4% (Mayfield), 73.1% (Purdy)

Brock Purdy got the best out of Jauan Jennings, Kendrick Bourne and Demarcus Robinson in similar situations. Now, he gets an albeit older Evans. So, while there is risk of an underwhelming season, Evans' past profile and current situation have the potential for a hit as a post-hype sleeper.

The subtitle is mostly in jest, but the guy I'm going to suggest fits into the bucket of a guy who mostly got his steps in on Sundays instead of scoring points during '25. Anyway, assuming that a TE who showed the athletic prowess to be effective as a receiver can still do so a few years later is the right place to start.

Similar story to the RBs and WRs, the data indicates slight drops in receiving proficiency from TEs who returned to form. Their ecosystems tell the greater story. And I know I mentioned this team earlier, but a change at QB could mean all the difference for T.J. Hockenson.

It bears repeating, but I have no stake in the Vikings' future. As a Bengals fan, I hope we see y'all in the Super Bowl (and Cincinnati wins). But let's paint an accurate picture of Hockenson's last three years.

Target Share: 24.0% (2023), 18.1% (2024), 15.9%

First Downs per Route Run: 9.5%, 10.0%, 5.9%

Hockenson breaks out soon after landing in Minnesota, but tears his ACL in the playoffs. He then missed all of training camp as the team rebuilt around new QB Sam Darnold. Hockenson rejoined the team midstream in their march to the playoffs, displacing ancillary pass-catchers like Jalen Nailor. But the former Lion didn't have the offseason to refine his timing with Sam Darnold. And let's rehash the "McCarthy experience" from Hockenson's point of view.

Total Attempts: 37 (McCarthy), 29th (out of 32 QBs)

Passing Success Rate (when targeting TEs): 45.9%, 28th

So, McCarthy wasn't throwing that often, nor was he putting Hockenson in situations to win. Meanwhile, Murray ranked second or third in TE target rate for three consecutive seasons. Approximately 34% of his passes went to the TE position from 2023 to 2025. The rest of the league hovered around 23%. If we're willing to accept that the offense will take a step forward with Murray under center, Hockenson stands to be a beneficiary of the improvement.

Merchandise sales, sponsorships and premium live event opportunities have become major supplements to his WWE income.Orton has gone the more traditional route to build wealth in the WWE. He broke through in the early 2000s, becoming a main-event staple with characters like the Legend Killer and The Viper. Rhodes is known for his slick American Nightmare persona, complete with custom suits, wrestling gear and luxury accessories. More recent coverage has also focused on his taste for luxury homes, cars and watches.Orton has also built a reputation for a lavish lifestyle, including luxury real estate and expensive vehicles. His wealth has also allowed him to live a family-oriented lifestyle away from WWE television. But there is no regular checking of the current value of his properties, cars and investments against public records.So the big difference is less in a specific dollar amount, and more in the manner the fortunes were made. Rhodes' fortune has grown with his current WWE stardom and ties to AEW and commercial brands, while Orton has had over 20 years of wrestling income to accumulate his wealth. articles.title: Figure skating: Olympic champion Alysa Liu announces break from competition
articles.summary: Women's Olympic figure skating champion Alysa Liu confirms that she will not compete during the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Women's Olympic figure skating champion Alysa Liu has confirmed she will not compete during the 2026-27 season.

Liu, 21, became the first American female since 2002 to win Olympic gold in women's singles in February at the Milano Cortina Games, where she also helped the United States to claim gold in the team event.

But in a post on social media, she said she will be taking a break from competition to work on her technique, meaning she will miss March's World Championships in Finland.

"I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve. It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth," she wrote on Instagram.

"I'm gonna take the time to recalibrate, fine-tune things & whatnot. So fear not, I'll be back, & in the meantime I'll be rooting for my teammates near & far."

In a separate interview with US broadcaster NBC , external , Liu added: "Logically and emotionally and physically, this just makes the most sense.

"I will miss seeing the international competitors at all the international (competitions), but there will be more, so it's fine."

It is not the first break that Liu has taken from the sport.

A former child prodigy, Liu became the youngest US champion ever in 2019 at the age of 13.

However, she announced her retirement from the sport in 2022 when she was just 16, before making a sensational return - by being crowned world champion in her comeback year and then going on to Olympic glory.

articles.title: Dodgers make massive Shohei Ohtani announcement amid NL battle with Braves, Brewers
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are right in the midst of trying to claim the NL in the regular season. On Wednesday, a Shohei Ohtani possibility came to life that w...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers currently sit in second place in the NL, just one game behind the Milwaukee Brewers . However, they are in the middle of a big series against the Atlanta Braves after dropping the series opener Tuesday night.

Shohei Ohtani has spent the last month focusing solely on his hitting rather than pitching. That is because of a lingering knee injury that has kept him off the mound.

"The Los Angeles Dodgers have been without the pitching services of two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani for over a month as he battles an ongoing knee and biceps injury. The team decided to shut down Ohtani from pitching just before the All-Star break in the hope of managing the injury, but it has lingered ever since. Ohtani received a lubricant shot in his knee, but the injury hasn't healed in the manner that Los Angeles would like to see," SI's Matt Levine wrote.

The knee injury first surfaced in June when Ohtani was removed from a game.

"Shohei Ohtani exited today's game with what the team described as left knee inflammation, and though Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters in Pittsburgh he expects him back in the lineup as early as tomorrow, it's worth noting his history with that left knee," ESPN's Alden Gonzales posted.

On Wednesday, MLB insider Jon Morosi shared that Ohtani could potentially make his return to the mound this weekend if everything goes well during his bullpen session.

"Shohei Ohtani starting on the mound Sunday in Detroit is a "possibility," Dave Roberts told reporters. The Dodgers' pitching plans for the weekend hinge on Ohtani's work today, which will be either a bullpen session or facing live hitters in Atlanta," Morosi wrote.

This is exactly what Dodgers fans want to hear with the playoffs getting closer. Los Angeles is also in a jam-packed race for the two first-round byes, making Ohtani's potential return to the mound even more significant.

The Dodgers already have a stacked rotation, but adding Ohtani back into the mix would make them even more dangerous. With the battle for the top two spots in the NL potentially going down to the wire, this is exactly where Ohtani needs to be in his recovery.
