Jeremiyah Love won't be the only running back that the Cardinals are monitoring as they head into their Week 1 game against the Chargers.

Veteran James Conner is returning from a foot injury that ended his 2025 season and has limited his practice participation this summer. On Wednesday, head coach Mike LaFleur said that Conner has been making progress but that the team remains unsure if that progress will extend far enough for Conner to play in the opener.

"It's starting to creep up ," LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team's website.

Love is recovering from an ankle injury that will keep him out of practice this week. If neither back can go, Tyler Allgeier will be in line to be the lead back to kick off the regular season.

articles.title: Yankees’ key piece is flashing warning lights: ‘They beat our guys tonight’ | Klapisch
articles.summary: The surging Red Sox are only two games behind the Yankees in the loss column in the AL wild card race.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — The Yankees' frustrating 9-7 loss to the Astros was only minutes old, but the wheels were already in motion in the post-game clubhouse.

Reliever Fernando Cruz , who'd pitched poorly yet again, was at his locker when manager Aaron Boone and a trainer summoned him across the room. The reliever spoke quietly to both, then had a separate conversation with Jason Zillo, the Yankees media relations director and VP of Communications.

Finally, closer David Bednar came over to pat Cruz on the shoulder and offer words of encouragement.

It was only then that Cruz made himself available to the press. He spoke cryptically about the two-run home run he surrendered to Jeremy Pena , and a 6.75 ERA in August, before finally revealing the real culprit.

"This is the part of the year that's a marathon," Cruz said, before adding, "all these things come with our long season."

Translated: Cruz's arm is tired; at 54.2 innings, he's already exceeded last year's workload (48 innings) and is all but certain to surpass his career high (66.2 innings) in 2024.

All indications are Cruz is headed to the injured list today. His roster spot will be filled by Triple-A call-up Elmer Rodriguez, who will start against the Astros tonight.

For Wednesday's matchup versus the Astros, Yankees moneyline is listed at -115 on DraftKings . Our complete DraftKings Sportsbook review shows you how to navigate through their app.

Cruz's regression reveals a greater warning sign for the Yankees bullpen, which blew three leads to the Astros on Tuesday. Boone's circle of trust consists of three irreplaceable pieces – Bednar and set-up men Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn – all of whom are being heavily relied upon this summer.

There's a fine line between steady use and grinding a reliever into dust. The Yankees' success in the final 31 games of the regular season depends on whether Boone can avoid crossing that divide.

Cruz is the first casualty, but Headrick, who leads all MLB relievers with 68 appearances, was suspiciously ineffective against Houston , too. Is he also showing signs of fatigue?

It's not an unreasonable question. Headrick lasted only two-thirds of an inning in the eighth, allowing four of the six batters he faced to reach base. In all, Headrick was charged with three runs, which put the game out of reach for the Yankees. It was his worst outing of the season.

Although Headrick insists he feels fine – "sometimes you don't make pitches when you want to, that's baseball" - the ease with which the Astros pummeled him had to be unsettling for Boone.

The manager was the first to admit, "they beat our guys tonight."

"I was reluctant to even use (Headrick)," Boone said. "We'll pick our spots…we're paying attention to that."

Here's the red flag: the Yankees have relied heavily on their bullpen since losing Aaron Judge in May. That success - a 3.05 ERA, second in the majors - has come at a cost.

Now the real crunch is just around the corner. The Yankees blew a chance to pull within two games of the first place Rays – who lost for the eighth time in 12 games in Detroit Tuesday night.

Meanwhile, Boston has crept to within two games of the Yankees in the loss column in the wild card race.

The biggest series of the season will take place this weekend against the Sox. It'll be a four-game showdown, and it's not enough the Sox are on a roll. They'll be especially dangerous with the expected return of slugger Roman Anthony on Friday. He's been out for 60 games with a partially torn tendon in his right ring finger.

The news isn't all bad for the Yankees, though. Assuming Rodriguez gets the ball tonight against Houston, he'll be riding a gust of momentum. He's allowed just four earned runs in his last 26 innings (1.38 ERA) at Triple-A. More importantly, Rodriguez, who's had trouble controlling his 100-mph fastball, has walked only one batter in his last 12 innings.

Also, it looks like Max Fried's rehab from a left elbow bone bruise is complete. Boone said it's likely the lefthander will start one of the two games in Saturday's doubleheader against Boston.

What's missing, of course, is Judge, who'll need another two weeks before he's re-activated. The captain's return will be an unquantifiable boost to the offense, not to mention the morale in the clubhouse. But it's worth noting how quickly Luis Garcia has

turned into a middle of the order weapon.

He went 4-for-5 with three RBIs, including a two-run HR in the fifth inning. Including his output with the Nationals before the Yankees acquired him at the trade deadline, Garcia now has 27 home runs on the season.

He's left-handed, smart, strong - and disciplined enough to say "I try not to think about it" when asked about how close the right field porch feels.

"If you do, you get too long (in your swing)," Garcia said. "It can change your swing and affect you negatively."

Pairing Garcia with a healthy Judge and Cody Bellinger is Boone's fever dream down the stretch. But first things first: the bullpen has to be nursed through the treacherous final weeks of late August.

Ironically, the Yankees were feeling confident about that very issue before the Astros ambushed them.

"I think (Boone) has kind of evolved in his bullpen utilization," pitching coach Matt Blake told Newsday's David Lennon. "Obviously his strength is communicating with the guys and understanding them."

Boone is indeed a smart guy. But recognizing the dog days is one thing - navigating them is another.

They're here and have already claimed one reliever.

articles.title: Rehabbing Yankees starter ‘definitely itching’ to  return to help beleaguered  bullpen
articles.summary: Starter Clarke Schmidt, who is rehabbing from his second Tommy John surgery in July 2025, says he’s “definitely itching” to come back
articles.body:
The beleaguered Yankees ' bullpen has been stretched thin this season as the team has struggled to score runs without Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton.

The pen took another hit Tuesday night when Fernandez Cruz was ineffective in his appearance in a 9-7 loss to the Houston Astros , and appears headed to the injured list today, per NJ.com's Bob Klapisch.

Starter Clarke Schmidt , who is rehabbing from his second Tommy John surgery in July 2025, says he's "definitely itching" to come back during the regular season and pitch out of the pen.

Yankees -1.5 run line is currently at +168 on FanDuel for Wednesday's game against Houston. Our in-depth FanDuel Sportsbook review provides a helpful guide on how to navigate their app.

"It's definitely gonna be nerve-wracking, but it's gonna be exciting," Schmidt told Meredith Marakovits of the YES Network following a live bullpen session Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. "It's been a while since I've competed and been on a game mound, so I'm definitely itching."

Schmidt pitched to bench coach Brad Ausmus and other batters during his bullpen session.

"I thought [my stuff] was good," he said. "...I was really happy with the shapes and the consistency of it."

Schmidt said a rehab assignment in the minors is expected next before he re-joins the team as a reliever.

"I think it's more of an inning-allotment type deal and pitch-count type deal," he said. "...And then also get used to the usages and get the pitch count up as much as we can."

He added: "There's definitely a plan in place."

Asked if he expects to come out of the bullpen during the season, Schmidt said, "Yes, 100%, I think that's been my goal from Day One. I want to be able to compete this year. I want to get innings under my belt before a full season next year.

"And I want to back get out there in the regular season, especially before playoffs and things really start picking up. Get the ball rolling a little bit and get back out there as quick as I can, and obviously competing at the Major League level was my No. 1 goal this year....

The Yankees' bullpen has been one of the team's biggest weapons this season, and it has pitched to a 3.05 ERA. But in the dog days of August, the pen is wearing down.

The pen blew three different leads on Tuesday night.

Depending on his conditioning, Schmidt could be a welcome addition come September.

"I think he could really help us. When he's on his game he's got a lot of weapons," Boone said.

articles.title: SEC reveals stiff penalties for teams recruiting pro players back to college
articles.summary: Here's a look at the SEC's reported new punishments.
articles.body:
As conferences try to determine how to handle teams attempting to bring professional players back to college, the SEC has decided on a punishment for violating the rules.

After SEC presidents met to discuss the situation, the conference came up with harsh penalties if teams try to play former professionals during the college season. Unlike many of the NCAA's penalties for violating rules, these SEC punishments are targeted specifically at those in charge of the program.

Thus far, just one school has really pushed to allow pros onto its college teams, and this update should make it less likely that more teams get involved. Here's a look at the SEC's reported new punishments.

Matt Norlander of CBS Sports reports that the SEC has decided on penalties for teams that recruit pro players back to the college game. Those penalties include:

Suspending the head coach for half a season

Revoking voting privileges on business matters within the SEC

Fining the program 50 percent of the sport's annual budget

Retaining the right to enforce additional penalties as decided by commissioner

These penalties are the first known punishments for this kind of violation as conferences address the ongoing issue of certain professional players potentially receiving eligibility to return to school. This largely applies to football, men's basketball and women's basketball, the three sports most likely to see teams try to recruit recent professionals.

What has the SEC said about schools allowing former pros to return to college?

The SEC has been pretty staunch in remaining against teams recruiting pros back to college. On Monday, the conference released a statement stating that "college sports is for college athletes."

Then, after the SEC presidents met to discuss the matter, the conference released another statement breaking down which players are ineligible from returning to college. That includes players who declared for a draft and never withdrew in time, and players who signed any kind of contract with a professional team.

Lawyers of players who received an extra year of eligibility are expected to challenge the SEC's decision in court.

"The SEC's actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders," lawyer Ryan Downton told Pete Thamel . "It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur of the moment rules in response to Courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level."

Considering previous rulings in this situation, it certainly would not be a surprise to see a judge overrule the SEC's decision. However, each of the conferences appear to be in lockstep regarding forbidding pros from returning to the college game.

Which SEC schools have attempted to sign former pros

Thus far, LSU is the only team to successfully recruit former pros back to college. The football team has signed three players, including tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who was in training camp with the Browns, while the basketball team has recruited former St. John's star RJ Luis after he went undrafted in the 2025 NBA Draft.

articles.title: Bennedict Mathurin to sign with Pelicans, face Pacers in season opener
articles.summary: Bennedict Mathurin will reportedly sign a two-year contract with the Pelicans for similar money to Kelly Oubre; who should the Pacers have signed?
articles.body:
The Pacers will get to see old friend Bennedict Mathurin again in their season opener.

The Pacers ' third-leading rookie scorer in franchise history will sign a two-year, $16 million contract with the New Orleans Pelicans , ESPN's Shams Charania reported Wednesday morning. Mathurin was traded to the Clippers as part of the February deal that brought Ivica Zubac to Indiana , and the Clippers have an opportunity to match the Pelicans' offer as a restricted free agent, but Charania and Jake Fischer of the Stein Line reported that the Clippers will work to make sure the deal works out and Mathurin goes to New Orleans .

The Pacers play the Pelicans in New Orleans on Oct. 21.

Former Pacer Bennedict Mathurin through the years

The Pacers selected Mathurin with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2022 draft, making him the Pacers' highest selection since Rik Smits was taken No. 2 overall in 1988. He responded by scoring the third-most points by a rookie in the Pacers' NBA history with 16.7 per game and a total of 1,302 points. Only Clark Kellogg and Chuck Person scored more as Pacers rookies. Mathurin also became the first Pacers rookie since Smits to be named first-team All-Rookie.

In the next three-plus seasons, Mathurin struggled to connect with the high-paced, ball-movement driven offense built around All-Star point guard Tyrese Haliburton as he is more of an isolation, one-on-one scorer by nature. However, when they needed someone to put his head down and go get a bucket -- particularly someone off the bench -- Mathurin was often the answer. He averaged 16.1 points per game in nearly four seasons with the Pacers. That included 17.6 points per game in 2025-26 when he often started on a squad that was snakebit by injuries and 16.1 per game on the 2024-25 team that reached the NBA Finals. He averaged a more modest 11.0 points per game in the 2025 playoffs -- he missed the 2024 postseason with a torn labrum -- but he cracked the 20-point mark five times in those playoffs with 20 in a Game 4 win over the Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals and 27 in a Game 3 win over the Thunder in the Finals.

The Pacers and Mathurin apparently couldn't agree on terms for a potential extension beyond his rookie-scale deal, which ended at the end of this season so he was an obvious piece to include in the Zubac trade to be able to match salary. The Pacers also sent center Isaiah Jackson and three draft picks to the Clippers including, conditionally, their 2026 first-round pick. The Pacers would have kept the selection if it landed in the top four or from 10-30, but it landed at No. 5 and the Clippers used the selection to pick Keaton Wagler .

Mathurin had struggles with the Clippers which obviously hurt his market value going into restricted free agency. He averaged 17.4 points per game in 26 games with Los Angeles , but shot just 42.6% from the floor -- worse than any of his seasons with the Pacers -- and made just 20.7% of his 3-pointers (17 of 82).

Are the Pacers better with Kelly Oubre or Bennedict Mathurin ?

The Pacers ended up signing a wing to effectively replace Mathurin for about the same money, giving Kelly Oubre Jr. $17 million over two years. Oubre might not have Mathurin's scoring potential and he's 30 while Mathurin just turned 24 in June.

However, the 6-8 Oubre gives the Pacers' more positional versatility than the 6-5 Mathurin. He's a much more accomplished defender and still a very good scorer. Over 11 seasons, he's averaged 13.3 points per game and averaged at least 14 per game in each of the last eight seasons with a high-water mark of 20.3 in 2022-23. He's also averaged at least 1.0 steals per game in each of the last nine seasons and with a 7-foot wingspan, he can guard any position from point guard to power forward. Mathurin may have more ability to create offense for himself and others, but Oubre can score off the bounce, from outside and in transition and can make plays on the defensive end that create offense.

articles.title: Richard Childress Racing Announces 2027 O’Reilly Auto Parts Series Lineup
articles.summary: Richard Childress Racing announced its 2027 driver lineup for the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series. Chandler Smith and Carson Brown make up the two-car team.
articles.body:
Richard Childress Racing has revealed its NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series driver lineup for the 2027 season. Chandler Smith will field the No. 21 Chevrolet, while Carson Brown will pilot the No. 2 Chevrolet. Both drivers will compete for a NOAPS championship on a full-time basis next year.

Smith is a three-time O'Reilly Auto Parts Series winner and a nine-time victor in the Craftsman Truck Series. He last raced in the NOAPS full-time in 2024 for Joe Gibbs Racing before moving down to the Craftsman Truck Series, where he currently competes for Front Row Motorsports.

The deal to drive for RCR is a multi-year agreement for Smith.

Brown currently competes part-time in the NOAPS for Jordan Anderson Racing. The 18-year-old is a one-time winner in the ARCA Menards Series after eight career starts.

Brown's deal, too, is part of a multi-year agreement.

Richard Childress releases statement on driver lineup

In a statement by RCR , car owner Richard Childress said Smith has earned the opportunity to drive the No. 21 car in 2027.

"He has shown throughout his career that he knows how to win, he knows how to compete and he understands what it takes to be successful at this level. We've watched him develop, and we believe he has all the tools to be a great fit at RCR. The No. 21 has a lot of history with our organization, and we're excited to put Chandler in that car and give him the opportunity to continue building his career with us," Childress said.

Childress also spoke highly of Brown , saying that it is not just what the youngster has produced on the track that has impressed the organization, but also his character and work ethic is something that the team looks forward to seeing.

"He has earned this opportunity through his performance and the way he approaches his development. Whelen has been a tremendous partner for RCR, and we're excited to have Carson represent the company and help us continue the work we've done together in support of important causes and highlight the industry-defining safety solutions that Whelen proudly builds, designs and manufactures in America," Childress said.

Richard Childress Racing's current drivers in the NOAPS

Austin Hill and Jesse Love are RCR's current drivers in the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, with Hill behind the wheel of the No. 21 Chevrolet and Love in the No. 2 machine.

Hill is a 16-time winner in the series, including two victories in 2026. This week, the 32-year-old signed an agreement with RCR to pilot the No. 33 Chevrolet full-time in the Cup Series beginning in 2027. Hill has been the fill-in driver in the Cup Series for RCR in the wake of the sudden passing of Kyle Busch.

Love captured last year's O'Reilly Auto Parts Series championship for RCR, the organization's first series title since 2019. Next year, Love will take his talents to the Cup Series when he gets behind the wheel of the No. 21 Wood Brothers Racing Ford, replacing Josh Berry.

articles.title: Root shows off-field leadership - now for on-field
articles.summary: Joe Root has shown himself to be the off-field leader England need - now comes a chance to show his credentials as captain on-field.
articles.body:
At the back of the Compton Stand at Lord's is an enormous picture of Ben Stokes.

In the snap, Stokes unleashes a bouncer to a flinching Mohammed Siraj, the India tailender. It was taken during England's heart-stopping 22-run win on this ground last summer.

England's defeat of India was all about Stokes. He made contributions with the bat in both innings, ran out Rishabh Pant with a direct hit and put in a trademark marathon bowling spell on the final day. Stokes came to the post-match media conference with blood seeping through his sock.

Throughout Stokes' tenure as England captain, the question loomed of how anyone would eventually go about succeeding him.

For better or worse, Stokes became the all-encompassing figure in the team, for his performances on the field and what he said or did off it. It was hard to imagine how anyone could emerge from his shadow without having their leadership compared to the talismanic all-rounder.

England are little more than a week into the post-Stokes era and there is already no doubt about the strength of leadership at the helm. This is Joe Root's team now.

The last thing Root would have wanted at the beginning of his second reign as skipper was the Brydon Carse controversy.

Yet, the Yorkshireman has shown himself to be the captain English cricket needs, yet probably does not deserve.

Root's measured, assured and honest address to the media at Lord's on Tuesday was the most impressive display of leadership from anyone connected with the England team in a long time.

Perhaps Root is helped by the circumstances. If Brendon McCullum was still around, he would have been pushed in front of cameras, but McCullum has gone and his replacement Stephen Fleming is yet to arrive. It leaves Root as unquestionably the man in charge.

In terms of Root's second coming as skipper, the off-field part might be the easy bit. It is on the field where he now has a point to prove.

He said as much last week before the Headingley Test - that the biggest challenge in resuming the captaincy was overcoming the perceptions others have of his leadership.

It is not that Root was an awful captain first time around - far from it. It is just the abiding memory is an awful ending of only one win from 17 matches, a horror run that left Root and his team broken.

Leeds was a dream restart, an innings win over Pakistan wrapped up inside three days.

But the one-sided nature of that victory did not give Root room to show what kind of on-field captain he will be this time around. His best act at Headingley was to win the toss and, after Ollie Robinson took a wicket with the first ball of the match, England were on top.

There have been glimpses of what the New Root could become.

Stokes' preference for naming an England team two days before a Test has gone, at least for now. England are likely to be unchanged at Lord's, though that will not be confirmed until the toss.

Root has removed himself from first slip and now fields at mid-off. It may only be a temporary move, but it puts him closer to his bowlers. On the first morning at Headingley, Root yanked a wayward Jofra Archer from the attack after only two overs. It is hard to imagine he would have done the same to either Stuart Broad or James Anderson.

There was a hint of funkiness in the field, albeit an overhang from Root's first spell as captain. The dismissal of Azan Awais in Pakistan's second innings was the eighth time a seamer under Root has had a catch taken at leg slip - the most of any captain since such data began being collected in 2006.

Asked what the difference was between the captaincy of Stokes and Root, fast bowler Josh Tongue said: "It's very chilled out there." Tongue probably did not mean to imply Root brings a greater calmness than Stokes, yet few would argue he has taken the intensity down a notch or two.

For all the impressive media conferences, bowling changes and leg slips, Root will be judged on results, and a win this week would give England their first series triumph since 2024.

There will be plenty of attention on the Lord's pitch, so heavily criticised after England's win against New Zealand. On Wednesday, Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) chairman Mark Nicholas and director of cricket Rob Lynch were seen taking a good look at the surface.

Pakistan should be better than their showing at Headingley, mainly because they cannot get much worse. They are boosted by the return of captain Babar Azam from a hand injury and have won the previous two Tests they have played here.

England will want to build on the green shoots of recovery that sprouted in Leeds.

Jordan Cox impressed at number three and is highly rated by the management. There could be a logjam in the top order when Jacob Bethell returns to fitness, so all of Cox, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence and Jamie Smith will want to ensure they are not squeezed out.

Root said his quartet of fast bowlers "do not know how good they can be". That foursome now have the opportunity to show they can be England's first-choice attack in a range of conditions. It is a bad time for Carse to put himself out of the picture.

As for Root, no man has more runs or hundreds on this ground. Now he returns as the captain, already leading by example this week.

"When you have the privilege of being a leader within a team, you want to build something bigger than just winning," he said. "I feel like I didn't do that very well first time around.

"There's a lot to look forward to, there's a lot to work hard towards. I guess that's the fun side of it."

For Root and his players, following the past few days, the fun side will simply be returning to playing cricket.
authors: Stephan Shemilt - Cricket Correspondent at Lord's

articles.title: Owen Hunt on Division 1 schools' radar
articles.summary: Aug. 26—VALLEY CITY, N.D. — Owen Hunt is getting Division 1 attention — and he's only a junior in high school. "This summer has been very exciting in my recr...
articles.body:
Aug. 26—VALLEY CITY, N.D. — Owen Hunt is getting Division 1 attention — and he's only a junior in high school.

"This summer has been very exciting in my recruitment, with schools being able to contact me personally now," Hunt said. "I have had great talks with schools like NDSU (North Dakota State University), SDSU (South Dakota State University), UND (University of North Dakota) and the University of Minnesota."

Hunt plays football for the Valley City High School program. The University of North Dakota offered Hunt a spot with the Fighting Hawks this summer.

"As coaches, we are very proud of how Owen has carried himself," Valley City head coach Chad Smith said. "Obviously, he has a lot of schools looking at him being 6-foot-5-inch, 300 pounds.

"We challenge him to be our leader, effort man, and voice in the locker room," he said. "He is a good kid, the next steps for him are to continue to do the little things, hand placements, footwork, and taking his game to the next level. He ... has a lot of football in front of him. I am truly excited to see how much his game can keep maturing this season."

Hunt is the son of Valley City High School athletic director Rob Hunt. A native of Cavalier, North Dakota, Rob Hunt played collegiate football at NDSU, then played professional football in the NFL for four seasons.

"My dad has been one of my biggest motivators during my high school career," Hunt said. "I've always wanted to do what he did, and he helps push me to achieve it."

Hunt said he has always been around football, but the first time he played was in 2020 as a fifth grader for Valley City's Thunder team.

In the last six years, he's grown — mentally and physically.

Last season, Hunt logged 40 tackles — seven solo and 33 assisted and a blocked punt for a safety. Offensively, he lined up a center, guard and tackle. Smith said he is expecting Hunt to play more of a tackle position this year.

"This past year has been some of my biggest growth as a player," Hunt said. "I've found that the weight room has been a huge part of this growth and that it's not just about the weight on the bar but just becoming a better athlete."

At the end of his summer training, Hunt was able to squat 435 pounds, bench press 335 pounds and clean 275 pounds.

Hunt and the Hi-Liners began practices on Aug. 6. The team saw its first competition on Aug. 21 against Velva/Drake-Anamoose. Valley City dropped 44-6 to the Aggies.

"I believe our team has a lot of opportunities for growth and development, with our team having a lot of young talent," Hunt said. "I think our biggest strength this year will be all of our young players that are coming through. In the time we have met this summer, they have been willing to be coached. I've seen good team connections develop over the summer."
authors: Katie Ringer, The Jamestown Sun, N.D.

articles.title: ‘We’ll be there to find it:’ Inside All Hail Media’s partnership with Robert Morris
articles.summary: RMU will be the focus of a roughly six-episode series produced by All Hail
articles.body:
Mid-major basketball programs and content creators have a lot in common.

They're both constantly trying to generate interest, engage an audience and develop revenue streams in order to survive in their current state. Robert Morris is turning those commonalities into a partnership with content creator Cullen Honohan and his five-person team at All Hail Media.

The program reached out to Honohan, who lives in Pittsburgh, this offseason to produce content around the team, essentially giving him a mandate to think outside the box. The result was an agreement to put All Hail's logo on the RMU uniform in exchange for a dedicated content series.

Honohan says that RMU basketball will become the main focus of the All Hail YouTube channel – which boasts 372,000 subscribers – with around six episodes produced and released throughout the season. They will supplement it with short-form content on All Hail's TikTok and Instagram pages, which have 1 million and 462,000 followers, respectively.

The first video, titled " I Rebuilt An Unknown College Basketball… (IN REAL LIFE) " is already out on YouTube. It introduces the team and lays the groundwork for the content plan.

"They're like 'we want to do something that nobody else has done before," Honohan said of RMU's pitch to him.

As a content creator, Honohan says that his 'core' is to tell positive basketball stories.

His content is primarily access-based. He posts all-access tours at top basketball prep schools and colleges, embarks on days in the life with top high school and college players, and more content of that ilk.

"We want to find the best stories in basketball," Honohan told Mid-Major Madness . "Find the best athletes, the top talent, the underdog players, the kids that might not have it all yet, but with the right tweaks and the right storytelling platform, we can kind of get there."

Much of All Hail's top-performing content on YouTube centers around stories with inherently broad appeal. The top seven most-viewed videos feature two abnormally tall teenagers, Montverde Academy, Tyran Stokes, AJ Dybantsa, Harvard University and Allen High School – Texas' largest public school.

"There's been radical change to college sports in general over the last four to five years," RMU head coach Andrew Toole said to USA Today . "How can we continue to adapt to the new landscape? I think content creators are part of that. It, I think, can help our players continue to become more attractive, and build a bigger brand and have a better experience."

Robert Morris isn't as catchy on a YouTube thumbnail. It's a winning program, but it's not a click machine by itself. Honohan knows that, and understands the risk involved, but can lean on some of his previous experience as well.

He said that for many of his videos, coaches and players will reach out to him asking him to find the story, and he'll put together something interesting. With the amount of time he'll be spending with Robert Morris, he's confident he can find the story that will resonate.

"The more time you spend, every program has something unique going on," he said. "Every program has something to offer, whether that's a unique player, a unique journey, a Cinderella run, we'll be there to find it."

This also isn't the first time that All Hail has made a series like this in the Pittsburgh area. Its most recent long-term project was a six-part series following 'unknown' high school player Luca Federico in an attempt to get him ranked by recruiting services, and offered by colleges. Federico eventually did attract high-major offers, but Honohan credits that to Federico's development as a player more so than the content. Nevertheless, the YouTube series got over 1.2 million views.

Honohan also pushed locally to build Federico's personal brand. All Hail put up 500 wanted posters in Pittsburgh telling people to follow his Instagram and pushed hard for local media attention. While he gained nearly 20,000 Instagram followers, All Hail fell short of the stated goal of getting Federico to 50,000.

"Show some of the interaction between players and coaches," Toole said. "Show the experience that our players have in a way that they might not have been able to see before. And I think that can attract some of the right people, not only to our program, but then also to our university as a whole."

With RMU, the local push becomes an even bigger focus, because much of his geographically scattered core audience won't be able to have quite as much of an impact on the success of the series as a locally-centered one. So he has to change his approach.

"Kids that are scrolling on Instagram and on TikTok, they're not going to be the same person that's donating to a school or running a business here in Pittsburgh that might want to be an in-person sponsor in the arena this season," Honohan said. "So, we're definitely going to have to tweak it in a sense of there's going to have to be different media that comes out about this. It's not solely going to be reliant on our social media platforms, which will be new to us."

All Hail is going to put up billboards in downtown Pittsburgh and put on events with local celebrities that will help make RMU "pop" locally.

And there's already local impact and reach. Honohan says he was stopped at a coffee shop by an "older gentleman" who asked him about Robert Morris and the partnership.

"I (usually) never get asked about what I do from anybody over probably the age of 20," Honohan said. "I'm excited to see how we can keep blending (the alumni base and older demographic in the city) into what we're doing."

Honohan is also leaning on All Hail's connections, and his connections through his management at The Team . He says that "a few different companies" will be working with Robert Morris this season that haven't previously because of the content.

And the core content, he hopes, will push people towards the program both locally and nationally.

"The stories aren't just going to be (vlogging with the team)," Honohan said. "The stories are essentially about how we can turn people in the city into long-term RMU fans."

articles.title: Chris Olave's new contract includes unique guarantee protections
articles.summary: The Saints included language in Chris Olave’s extension allowing injury guarantees to be voided for two specific pre-existing medical conditions.
articles.body:
New details of Chris Olave 's contract extension reveal an unusual layer of protection for the New Orleans Saints . The provision addresses two serious medical issues the star wideout has experienced during his four-year NFL career.

The contract identifies "concussions and respiratory pulmonary embolism" as pre-existing conditions, according to NewOrleans.Football's Nick Underhill. ESPN's Katherine Terrell confirmed that if Olave is no longer medically cleared to play football because of either condition, his injury guarantees can be voided. The process requires Saints doctors to consult an independent third-party specialist before the team's doctor makes the final decision on Olave's medical clearance. That determination is considered "final and binding," and all injury guarantees would become void if Olave cannot be cleared because of either listed condition — including a deterioration or aggravation of one.

Of course, the language directly reflects what Olave's medical history has shown. Multiple concussions limited him to just eight games in 2024. The 26-year-old WR has suffered, at least, four concussions during his professional career — and he dealt with at least one concussion during his college career at Ohio State. Doctors detected a blood clot in Olave's lung before the Saints' 2025 season finale against the Atlanta Falcons . He was expected to make a full recovery, though the Saints limited his participation during portions of the offseason while he remained on blood thinners. Ahead of training camp, Olave was fully cleared, and he remains a daily participant in practice.

Olave and the team agreed to a four-year extension carrying a base value of $124 million and a maximum value of $132 million. The agreement contains just over $90 million in total guarantees, with around $52.7 million fully guaranteed when the deal was signed, according to Over the Cap . Despite the injury protections, New Orleans still made a significant long-term commitment to Olave after a career-best 2025 season. He caught 100 passes for 1,163 yards and nine touchdowns while earning second-team All-Pro honors. It gives the Saints protection against the two medical conditions that have most threatened Olave's availability, while also rewarding him with a contract that reflects his production.

articles.title: Report: Bradley Barcola ‘not pushing’ to leave PSG amid Liverpool interest
articles.summary: Bradley Barcola to Liverpool: PSG Await Improved Bid as Transfer Talks Enter Key StageLiverpool’s pursuit of Bradley Barcola appears to be moving into a deci...
articles.body:
Bradley Barcola to Liverpool : PSG Await Improved Bid as Transfer Talks Enter Key Stage

Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola appears to be moving into a decisive phase, with PSG now expecting an improved offer inside the next 24 to 48 hours. According to Julien Laurens on ESPN , personal terms have already been agreed with the France international, leaving club-to-club negotiations as the central issue.

That, on the surface, is a significant step. When personal terms are in place this early, it usually points to alignment on the player side and confidence from the buying club that a deal can still be struck. Liverpool have clearly identified Barcola as a priority target, and their work behind the scenes reflects that.

The most notable element in the latest update is the suggestion that PSG are anticipating another approach rather than shutting the door. That matters. It indicates discussions remain active and that Liverpool have not been discouraged from returning with improved terms.

There is, however, an important nuance in the player's position. As Laurens reported, "Liverpool agreed personal terms with Barcola, who has been the priority signing for the Merseyside club all summer, some time ago," and "However, Barcola, who has two years left on his contract, is not forcing a move out of the French capital and is not averse to staying put."

That does not automatically weaken Liverpool's hand, though it does remove one common source of pressure in late-window business. If a player is not actively agitating for a transfer, the selling club can afford to be firmer in its valuation and timing. PSG may feel that gives them a stronger platform in negotiations, especially after strengthening other areas of their squad.

Liverpool transfer strategy now faces one clear route

Liverpool's options elsewhere also appear limited. Their efforts to sign Yankuba Minteh have been resisted, with Brighton standing firm at £80m. In practical terms, that only sharpens the focus on Barcola. For Liverpool, this looks increasingly like a deal to complete rather than a conversation to revisit at a later date.

There is also a broader market reality at play. Barcola has two years left on his contract, which means this window represents a major opportunity for PSG to secure top value if they decide to sell. Leave it any later and the balance can shift quickly.

From Liverpool's perspective, the expectation of an improved bid suggests intent, momentum and a willingness to find a compromise. The challenge now is whether that next offer lands close enough to PSG's demands to take the transfer into its final stages.

As an anxious Liverpool supporter, this is the kind of update that gives you hope and stress in equal measure. On one hand, agreeing personal terms with Bradley Barcola feels huge. You do not get that far without serious groundwork, and it tells you the player is open to the move. On the other hand, hearing that he is not pushing to leave PSG immediately raises the fear that this could drag on right until the deadline.

That is the part supporters hate. Once a deal becomes the clear priority, every day without a breakthrough feels loaded with risk. Liverpool seem to have narrowed their focus, especially if Brighton are holding hard on that £80m price for Minteh, so there is a sense now that the club almost has to get this one over the line.

Barcola makes sense stylistically, in profile and in long-term value. He feels like the sort of forward who could lift the attack and grow quickly at Anfield. But supporters will also worry about PSG dictating the pace and price of the discussion while Liverpool wait for the right opening.

Ultimately, this report reads like a transfer that is alive and advancing, but still vulnerable to late complications. That is why fans will be watching the next 48 hours nervously, hoping Liverpool's next move is the one that finally gets it done.

articles.title: Ja’Marr Chase misses Bengals’ Wednesday practice

As expected, the Cincinnati Bengals held Ja'Marr Chase out of Wednesday's practice following an injury to his left knee on Tuesday.

The Bengals are already holding their starters out of Friday's preseason finale vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while there's over two weeks remaining until the regular-season opener vs. the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

For now, it does not appear Chase is in danger of missing the opener, but we'll have to see how treatment goes and how much swelling there is in the injured knee before a final determination is made.

articles.title: Roki Sasaki looks to continue his second half success
articles.summary: The Dodgers look to even up the series in Atlanta against the Braves, a series that could be key to which team owns one of the top two spots in the NL, which...
articles.body:
The Dodgers look to even up the series in Atlanta against the Braves, a series that could be key to which team owns one of the top two spots in the NL, which would give them that ever-so-important bye in the first round.

Currently, the Dodgers are one game behind the Milwaukee Brewers in wins, as the New York Mets came back in extras to also hand the Brewers a loss. Atlanta is three games behind L.A. with 77 wins.

The bottom of the lineup was key in the three runs scored in Tuesday night's game, and the top of the order needs to join in if the Dodgers wish to unleash more offense. The team will face AJ Smith-Shawver , a young righty who has only appeared in two games so far this season. He just returned after spending 14 months healing from Tommy John surgery and has joined the Braves rotation to give them a six-man staff to save some arm usage for the playoffs. In those two games this season he went 4.1 innings both times, allowing two earned runs in the first outing and four runs in the second outing. He has only seven strikeouts across those 8.2 innings.

Smith-Shawver leans on a curveball that breaks into lefty barrels, and the Dodgers could stack up to seven lefties against him. He lacks a reliable fading changeup that could potentially keep those lefties off balance.

The Dodgers did little to make the Braves bullpen work in Tuesday game and all arms should be available. The Dodgers could work to break the game open and get into the bullpen early, but bullpen usage may not matter as Chris Sale looms on Thursday.

Roki Sasaki will take the mound for the Dodgers. He hasn't earned the wins in any of his last three games, but he has looked much more solid, allowing only two runs in each of his last three outings, one of which was in Denver. Coming into last night's game, the Braves had only been averaging 1.3 earned runs against righties in their last 10 started by righties. After getting ahead of Glasnow in the first with three runs, Glasnow was able to shut them down pretty solidly the rest of the way. He ended up striking out seven, and Sasaki could rack up some K's himself.

articles.title: Holy Cross football seeks upset against Lehigh in season opener
articles.summary: Holy Cross football opens its season against defending Patriot League champion Lehigh in a high stakes matchup.
articles.body:
WORCESTER – For the first full season since 2018, the Holy Cross football team opens the year against a Patriot League opponent, defending PL champion Lehigh no less, so, for the Crusaders , the stakes are high from the start.

"As a competitor, it's one of those games you look forward to," HC senior linebacker Adam Due said before practice earlier this week at Kuzniewski Field. "We're excited for the opportunity we have in front of us."

The No. 11 Mountain Hawks visit Fitton Field at 3:30 p.m. Aug. 29 as the Patriot League kicks off a new era with the addition of Villanova and William & Mary, bringing membership to 10 schools.

The Crusaders were picked sixth in the PL preseason poll.

"Going against a top team in the country and the reigning Patriot League champs is about as good an opportunity you can get to see where we're at," Holy Cross third-year coach Dan Curran said. "Our guy are excited to go against such a quality opponent. The game is really meaningful and it's an unbelievable opportunity. We're going to make the most of it and go have some fun with it."

Aug. 29 is the earliest Holy Cross has opened a season in program history . The Crusaders are looking for their first win in the month of August (0-7 all-time).

Coming into 2026, the Crusaders are a driven and determined group. There are 33 new players, including 15 transfers, and HC's returners have moved on from the disappointment of last year's 3-9 finish. Five of the losses were by eight points or less.

"We don't focus on last year," junior wide receiver Ty Curran said. "We were so close last year; we know what we can do. We have the pieces now. I think we're going to have a lot of success. We're focused on a new team and new energy."

Holy Cross entered preseason camp with a three-man battle among senior Cal Swanson, junior David Lynch and sophomore Dom Campanile for the starting quarterback position.

Over the last couple weeks, Swanson and Lynch separated themselves in the competition for QB1. Dan Curran said earlier this week that the team would not be publicly naming the starter before the opener, but it is likely to be Lynch, a transfer from Pitt.

"There will be one guy who's going to take the majority of the snaps," Dan Curran said, "but I expect to see all three of those guys on the field at some point Saturday. All three have earned the right to get on the field."

In 2025, Holy Cross averaged just 20.5 points per game to rank seventh out of eight teams in the PL, but with additions to the offensive line as well as wide receiver and running back rooms, the Crusaders expect improvement on offense.

"We've all progressed so much," Ty Curran said. "We will be a completely different looking offense than last year. The big thing is how much more explosive we are – more big plays, more highlight plays, more flip-the-field type plays."

Lehigh, which is coming off a 12-0 regular season in 2025, has a new coach in Rich Nagy, who served as the Mountain Hawks' defensive coordinator for the last three years. Nagy replaced Kevin Cahill, who took over at Yale for Oxford's Tony Reno.

Under Nagy, Lehigh ranked in the top five nationally in five major defensive categories last year.

Among the Mountain Hawks' five returning All-PL selections and 13 starters from last year is senior running back Luke Yoder, the 2025 PL Offensive Player of the Year who rushed for 1,409 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2025.

In a 38-3 win over Holy Cross last season, the Mountain Hawks rolled up 344 yards on the ground.

"We have to stop the run," Dan Curran said. "They know it. We know it. We won't completely stop a player of that category, but we will try to minimize it and put them in a different situation. That will be the key and hopefully that will allow us to get some takeaways, minimize what they do offensively and give our offense some good possessions."

articles.title: Fever-Sky averages 3.31M viewers, most-watched regular-season WNBA game since 1997
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky game Sunday averaged 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock to make it the most-watched regular-season WNBA game since the lea...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky game Sunday averaged 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock to make it the most-watched regular-season WNBA game since the league's inaugural season in 1997.

It also was the third-most watched regular-season game ever and peaked at 3.82 million viewers. That is behind only the June 21-22, 1997 opening weekend games that featured the New York Liberty-Los Angeles Sparks (5.04 million) and Charlotte Sting-Phoenix Mercury (3.59 million), also both on NBC.

Caitlin Clark and the Fever continue to be the league's top draw. They also have set all-time viewing records this season for games on CBS, ESPN and Amazon Prime Video.

Against the Sky , Clark made a career-high eight 3-pointers and scored 37 points in the Fever's 113-90 victory. Teammate Kelsey Mitchell added 30.

That game was the first meeting since Chicago 's DiJonai Carrington fouled Indiana 's Sophie Cunningham on a breakaway in the Fever's 90-86 victory on Aug. 8. Carrington was ejected for the Flagrant 2 foul.

There were no such incidents between the two in the rematch.

But there was controversy. Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom attended as a spectator and was ejected in the third quarter after he and the Sky's Natasha Cloud exchanged words. Freedom has since been banned from Sky home games .

articles.title: Panthers rookie OT Monroe Freeling struggles mightily at joint practice vs. Texans
articles.summary: Panthers rookie OT Monroe Freeling might've had his "Welcome to the NFL" moment during Wednesday's joint practice with the Texans.
articles.body:
After this morning's joint practice with the Houston Texans , Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales started his press conference with two words . . . or two names— Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson . The star pass rushers led Houston's dominant defensive showing , accounting for most of the Texans' seven sacks against the Panthers offense.

The primary victim of their work seemed to be rookie offensive lineman Monroe Freeling, who's currently manning the right tackle position on Carolina's first-team unit. Canales, however, looked at the positive side of what went down.

"Oh, it's fantastic," he said of Freeling getting exposure to the likes of Hunter and Anderson. "This is what Monroe needs. As he works his fundamentals, his technique, all the little different things—it just gets magnified when you play two rushers like this."

Freeling, the 19th overall pick from this year's draft, may have been initially selected with designs of a reserve role here in 2026. But with longtime starting right tackle Taylor Moton now recovering from a blood clot in his lung, the rookie has been thrown into the fire.

Canales was later asked how Freeling can bounce back from getting torched by the Texans.

"It's just right to the film," he replied. "And it's good, and bad. As I talked to the group afterwards, these are such valuable opportunities—to be able to go against a new group with a different skill set, to be able to see those things.

"He'll go right into the film right now with Coach [Joe] Gilbert and the o-line, and they'll work on those things, clean it up and we'll go from there."

Freeling is also learning, or re-learning, the feel at right tackle. The 6-foot-7, 318-pounder was primarily a left tackle at the University of Georgia, having recorded 1,102 of his 1,369 offensive snaps on the blindside.

In perhaps adding to Canales' glass-half-full attitude, at least Freeling might've already gotten his "Welcome to the NFL" moment done and over with.
